title: Roots and patterns: how Arabic morphology works
text: Lesson overview In A1, you saw that ⁧كِتَاب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَبَة⁩ and ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ share the same three consonants. In this unit, that observation becomes a practical tool: the root ( ⁧الجِذْر⁩ ) carries a general idea, while the pattern ( ⁧الوَزْن⁩ ) turns it into a verb, a person, a place or an action. With around twenty common patterns, you can understand words you have never studied and find them in a dictionary. For anyone reading Arabic sources, this is the most useful skill at this level. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-01 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites Examination A1 exceeded (at least 70%, each section at least 60%) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 49–50 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-01), voice synthesis script, a root-ordered dictionary (Appendix C), session with the tutor in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. identify the root of a regular word by removing article, prefixes, long vowels and endings; 2. recognize the most frequent patterns and their value: fāʿil "Those who do" are: mafʿūl "what it suffers" mafʿal / mafʿala Place (s) of origin fiʿāla and faʿl The action shall be: mifʿāl The following definitions apply: faʿīl "Quality' is defined as: 3. build a family of words from a known root and guess the meaning of a new word from root and schema; 4. recognize when the root is weak or double and where to look for it; 5. find a word in a dictionary ordered by root; 6. read a vocalized text of 150 words and collect the words by root. Two-week plan. The root: an idea, not a word Almost all Arabic words of Arab origin can be divided into two parts that interweave: • root ( ⁧جِذْر⁩ ǧiḏr): Usually three consonants, sometimes four, that bring a general idea. No yes It says by itself and writes with separate letters: ⁧ك ت ب⁩ ; • the scheme ( ⁧وَزْن⁩ wazn, literally weight, measure inserts into the root and decides the category and a part of the meaning. Word = root + scheme. In ⁧كَاتِب⁩ the root is ⁧ك ت ب⁩ , the schema is consonant + ā + consonant + i + consonant Root General idea Words you already know ⁧ك ت ب⁩ write ⁧مَكْتَبَة⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ , ⁧كُتُب⁩ , ⁧كِتَاب⁩ , ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ ⁧د ر س⁩ study ⁧مُدَرِّسَة⁩ , ⁧مُدَرِّس⁩ , ⁧مَدْرَسَة⁩ , ⁧دَرْس⁩ , ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ ⁧ع م ل⁩ do, work ⁧عُمَّال⁩ , ⁧عَامِل⁩ , ⁧عَمَل⁩ , ⁧عَمِلَ⁩ ⁧س ك ن⁩ to live; Stay still ⁧يَسْكُنُ⁩ , ⁧سَكَنَ⁩ ⁧ج ل س⁩ sit down ⁧غُرْفَةُ الجُلُوسِ⁩ , ⁧مَجْلِس⁩ , ⁧جَلَسَ⁩ ⁧خ ر ج⁩ exit ⁧الخَارِجِيَّة⁩ , ⁧خَارِج⁩ , ⁧مَخْرَج⁩ , ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ ⁧د خ ل⁩ enter ⁧الدَّاخِلِيَّة⁩ , ⁧مَدْخَل⁩ , ⁧دَخَلَ⁩ ⁧ط ب خ⁩ Cooking ⁧مَطْبَخ⁩ , ⁧طَبَخَ⁩ Because you need it. In front of a new word in a title, the root immediately gives you the field of meaning; the scheme tells you if it is a person, a place, an action or a quality. Many times enough to understand; when it's not enough, the root is the address you search for in the dictionary (section 6). The foreign words ( ⁧بَرْلَمَان⁩ , ⁧بَنْك⁩ , ⁧فِيلْم⁩ ) and some very ancient words ( ⁧أَب⁩ , ⁧أُمّ⁩ ) do not have a recognizable pattern: they are learned as blocks. Roots of four consonants. You already know two of them: ⁧ت ر ج م⁩ in ⁧مُتَرْجِم⁩ and ⁧ه ن د س⁩ in ⁧مُهَنْدِس⁩ . They are few and follow their own patterns. 3. The diagram and the letters ⁧ف ع ل⁩ To indicate a pattern without tying it to a root, Arab grammars use the root ⁧ف ع ل⁩ Do not do this: ⁧ف⁩ stands for the first root consonant, ⁧ع⁩ for the second, ⁧ل⁩ for the third. Everything else (vowels, prefixes, doubles) belongs to the scheme. How to Find the Root Always proceed in the same order. 1. Remove what is not word: article ( ⁧ال⁩ ), conjunctions and combined prepositions ( ⁧وَ⁩ , ⁧فَ⁩ , ⁧بِـ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ , ⁧كَـ⁩ ), suffix pronouns ( ⁧ـهُ⁩ , ⁧ـهَا⁩ , ⁧ـهُمْ⁩ ...), gender loss and number ( ⁧ـة⁩ , ⁧ـات⁩ , ⁧ـُونَ⁩ , ⁧ـِينَ⁩ , ⁧ـَانِ⁩ ). 2. Remove the prefixes of the scheme: ⁧مَـ⁩ / ⁧مُـ⁩ (places, instruments, parts), ⁧تَـ⁩ / ⁧تِـ⁩ (action names such as ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ ), ⁧اِ⁩ / ⁧اِسْتِـ⁩ / ⁧اِنْـ⁩ (derived forms: ⁧اِجْتِمَاع⁩ , ⁧اِسْتِقْبَال⁩ ), ⁧أَ⁩ (plurality as ⁧أَقْلَام⁩ ), ⁧يَـ⁩ / ⁧تَـ⁩ / ⁧نَـ⁩ / ⁧أَ⁩ of the imperfect. 3. Remove internal long vowels ( ⁧ا⁩ , ⁧و⁩ , ⁧ي⁩ ) and doubling: almost always they are of the scheme. In ⁧كِتَاب⁩ the ⁧ا⁩ is of schema; in ⁧مُدَرِّس⁩ the ⁧ر⁩ doubled is only worth one ⁧ر⁩ of the root. 4. Three consonants remain: that is the root. If there are two left, go to the section 5. The Dictionary by Root Many bilingual Arabic dictionaries are sorted by root, not by the first letter of the word: to find ⁧مَعْلُومَات⁩ look for the root ⁧ع ل م⁩ And under that voice, you find the whole family. This is the case of Hans Wehr's Arabic-English dictionary, the most common reference (Appendix C): under each root the simple verb with the vowel of the imperfect and its action names, then the derived forms indicated with Roman numerals (II, III... X), then the names. How to use: 1. find the root with the section method 5; 2. search for the root in Arabic alphabetical order: first the first consonant, then the second, then the third ( ⁧ك ت ب⁩ comes before ⁧ك ث ر⁩ why ⁧ت⁩ comes before ⁧ث⁩ ); 3. inside the voice, look for the scheme: a participle (fāʿil, mafʿūl), a place (mafʿal) or an action name; 4. If you don't find anything, the root is probably weak or double: go back to section 6. Arabic alphabetical order, to remember for the search: ⁧ا ب ت ث ج ح خ د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ك ل م⁩ ⁧ن ه و ي⁩ . Many digital apps and dictionaries also search for the whole word. They are comfortable, but the root dictionary shows you the family and helps you remember: use it at least for important words. 8. Root and meaning: traps The root gives the field, not translation. Three frequent traps: 1. The meaning has specialized. ⁧جَامِعَة⁩ comes from ⁧ج م ع⁩ • bring together, but it means university; ⁧مَجْلِس⁩ comes from ⁧ج ل س⁩ "Sit down" means "consiglio," "assemble" ( ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ ). title: The perfect: full conjugation · first year budget
text: Lesson overview In A1-18 you learned the perfect to the singular, with ...noi and theirs, and some perfect irregular to memorize. In this unit complete the picture: all thirteen people, the three vowels of the base and, above all, the rule of the two bases that explains why ⁧قَالَ⁩ becomes ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ and ⁧مَشَى⁩ becomes ⁧مَشَيْتُ⁩ . By that rule, the verbs \"irregularÂ" stop being. The second week closes the first year with a budget for skill and plan of the year 2. Item Details Code A2-02 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites A2-01 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 51–52 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-02), voice synthesis script, progress log (Excel file), tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to combine a regular verb to the perfect in all persons, including women and duals; 2. explain the rule of the two bases and apply it to concave verbs ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧بَاعَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ ), defects ( ⁧مَشَى⁩ , ⁧دَعَا⁩ , ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ ) and verbs ⁧جَاءَ⁩ , ⁧رَأَى⁩ , ⁧رَدَّ⁩ ; 3. combine verbs with hamza ( ⁧أَخَذَ⁩ , ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ , ⁧قَرَأَ⁩ , ⁧بَدَأَ⁩ ) and those beginning with ⁧و⁩ ( ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ , ⁧وَضَعَ⁩ ); 4. grant the verb with singular, dual and plural subjects, before and after the verb; 5. recognize and use ⁧قَدْ⁩ and ⁧لَقَدْ⁩ with the perfect, as in the news; 6. tell a year or a trip to 90 words and understanding a story at moderate speed; 7. make the first year budget with measured data, skills for skill. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · One year of Arabic Last class of the first year. Salmā He's getting the point with the class. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧اِنْتَهَتِ السَّنَةُ الأُولَى! مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمْ هٰذِهِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧السَّنَةَ؟⁩ Salmā: intahati s-sanatu l-ūlā! māḏā faʿaltum hāḏihi s-sana? Salmā: It's finished in the first year! What did you do this year? ⁧دَرَسْنَا الحُرُوفَ وَالكَلِمَاتِ الأُولَى،⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَقَرَأْنَا نُصُوصًا كَثِيرَةً، وَكَتَبْنَا رَسَائِلَ⁩ ⁧وَتَقَارِيرَ.⁩ Lūkā: darasnā l-ḥurūfa wa-l-kalimāti l- ūlā, wa-qaraʾnā nuṣūṣan kaṯīratan, wa- katabnā rasāʾila wa-taqārīr. Luca: We studied the letters and the first words, we read many texts and we wrote letters and reports. ⁧وَأَنْتُمَا يَا يُوسُف وَسَمِير؟ هَلْ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧نَجَحْتُمَا فِي الاِمْتِحَانِ؟⁩ Salmā: wa-antumā yā Yūsuf wa- Samīr? hal naǧaḥtumā fī l-imtiḥān? SalmāAnd you two, Yūsuf and Samīr? Did you pass the test? ⁧نَعَمْ، نَجَحْنَا، وَسَمِير أَخَذَ أَحْسَنَ⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ ⁧نَتِيجَةٍ فِي الصَّفِّ!⁩ Yūsuf: naʿam, naǧaḥnā, wa-Samīr aḫaḏa aḥsana natīǧatin fī ṣ-ṣaff! Yūsuf: Yes, we have passed it, and Samīr He's got the best result in the class! ⁧مَبْرُوك! وَأَنْتُنَّ يَا مَارْيَا وَإِيلِينَا وَآنَّا؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧مَتَى بَدَأْتُنَّ؟⁩ Salmā: mabrūk! wa-antunna yā Māryā wa-Īlīnā wa-Ānnā? matā badaʾtunna? SalmāCongratulations! What about you, Maria, Elena and Anna? When did you start? ⁧بَدَأْنَا مَعًا فِي أُكْتُوبَرَ المَاضِي، وَمَا⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ ⁧تَرَكْنَا دَرْسًا وَاحِدًا!⁩ Māryā: badaʾnā maʿan fī uktūbara l- māḍī, wa-mā taraknā darsan wāḥidan! Maria: We started together last October, and we didn't skip a single lesson! ⁧وَالطُّلَّابُ الآخَرُونَ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-ṭ-ṭullābu l-āḫarūn? Salmā: What about the other students? ⁧سَافَرَ اثْنَانِ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ فِي الصَّيْفِ،⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَعَادَا بِكَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةٍ مِنَ الدَّارِجَةِ!⁩ Lūkā: sāfara ṯnāni ilā l-Maġribi fī ṣ- ṣayf, wa-ʿādā bi-kalimātin kaṯīratin mina d-dāriǧa! Two went to Morocco in the summer, and they came back with a lot of darija words! ⁧وَمَاذَا نَسِيتُمْ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-māḏā nasītum? Salmā: And what have you forgotten? ⁧لَا شَيْءَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ!⁩ … ⁧نَسِينَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: nasīnā… lā šayʾa, in šāʾa llāh! We forgot... nothing, if God wills! What to notice. Salmā use three different ⁧فَعَلْتُمْ⁩ (group or mixed), ⁧نَجَحْتُمَا⁩ (you two) ⁧بَدَأْتُنَّ⁩ (you women, at least three: for two women you use the dual, ⁧بَدَأْتُمَا⁩ ). ⁧اِنْتَهَتِ⁩ and support: before the article the tāʾ of ...lei... takes one (A1-18). ⁧عَادَا⁩ They're back (they two) is a dual, while ⁧سَافَرَ اثْنَانِ⁩ has the verb to the singular because it comes before the subject. ⁧أَحْسَنَ نَتِيجَةٍ⁩ The best result is: the construction is in A2-11. ⁧مَبْرُوك⁩ Congratulations, congratulations are said for an examination, a marriage, a new house; answer ⁧اللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ⁩ God bless you. ⁧أُكْتُوبَر⁩ is the name of the month in use in Egypt and Maghreb (A1-17). 2. Look at the suffix column: some start with a consonant (-you, -ta, -ti, -ti). tumā, -nā, -tum, -tunna, -na), others with a vowel (-a, -at, -ā, -atā, -ū). In front of the first the base ends with a sukūn (daras-tu); in front of the seconds the base ends with a vowel (darasa, darasat). This difference, which in regular verbs seems a detail, is the key to all weak verbs: keep it in mind for sections 5–7. Tricks to distinguish shapes. • -na -nā: ⁧دَرَسْنَ⁩ Darasna ... ⁧دَرَسْنَا⁩ darasnā "We" is the name of the company. Without vowels they are only distinguished by the final aliif. • -tum and -tunna: male is also the form of mixed groups: a man in a group of women is enough to - Tum. • -ā and -atā: the third-person duals are the form and form of the second-person duals, with -ā more: ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ → ⁧دَرَسَا⁩ , ⁧دَرَسَتْ⁩ → ⁧دَرَسَتَا⁩ . • The Alif changes: only -ū is written with an alif that is not pronounced ( ⁧دَرَسُوا⁩ ). -ā It's pronounced. 3. The vowel of the base and the verbs of the first year The basis of the perfect has vowel a, i or, more rarely, u on the second consonant. It is not derived from the meaning: one learns with the verb, together with the vowel of the imperfect. Type Perfect Imperfect First year verbs faʿala – yafʿulu   ⁧دَرَسَيَكْتُبُكَتَبَ⁩ ⁧طَلَبَ⁩ , ⁧تَرَكَ⁩ , ⁧حَدَثَ⁩ , ⁧حَضَرَ⁩ , ⁧ذَكَرَ⁩ , ⁧طَبَخَ⁩ , ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ , ⁧دَخَلَ⁩ , ⁧سَكَنَ⁩ , faʿala – yafʿilu   ⁧عَرَفَيَجْلِسُجَلَسَ⁩ ⁧حَمَلَ⁩ , ⁧فَقَدَ⁩ , ⁧رَجَعَ⁩ , faʿala – yafʿalu   ⁧فَتَحَيَذْهَبُذَهَبَ⁩ ⁧دَفَعَ⁩ , ⁧نَجَحَ⁩ , ⁧بَحَثَ⁩ , ⁧بَدَأَ⁩ , ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ , ⁧قَرَأَ⁩ , faʿila – yafʿalu   ⁧عَمِلَيَفْهَمُفَهِمَ⁩ ⁧سَمِعَ⁩ , ⁧شَرِبَ⁩ , faʿula – yafʿulu ⁧يَكْبُرُكَبُرَ⁩ (states and quality: ... become big, grow ...) The rule of A1-18 remains valid: if the perfect has the i, the imperfect has almost always the a. Verbs in faʿula almost always indicate a quality that is acquired ( ⁧كَبُرَ⁩ "Become big" ⁧صَعُبَ⁩ "To become difficult"): they are few and for now you just recognize them. The hamza is a consonant like the others: the verb is regular. It only changes the support of the hamza, according to the vowels nearby. How many? ⁧١. دَفَعُوا.⁩ ⁧٢. دَعَوْا.⁩ ⁧٣. دَرَسْتُنَّ.⁩ ⁧٤. قُلْتُمَا.⁩ ⁧٥. نَسِينَ.⁩ ⁧٦. جِئْنَا.⁩ ⁧٧. رَأَتْ.⁩ ⁧٨. خِفْتِ.⁩ ⁧٩. بَاعَتَا.⁩ ⁧١٠. رَدَدْنَ.⁩ Script C · The story of Hudā ⁧فِي الشَّهْرِ المَاضِي قَضَيْتُ أُسْبُوعًا فِي تُونِسَ عِنْدَ عَائِلَةِ أَبِي. وَصَلْتُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ، وَجَاءَ عَمِّي إِلَى⁩ ⁧المَطَارِ. فِي اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ مَشَيْنَا فِي المَدِينَةِ القَدِيمَةِ، وَأَخَذْنَا صُوَرًا كَثِيرَةً. يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْنِ فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي⁩ ⁧فِي السُّوقِ! خِفْتُ كَثِيرًا، لٰكِنَّ بَائِعًا وَجَدَهُ وَرَدَّهُ إِلَيَّ. فِي آخِرِ يَوْمٍ دَعَتْنَا عَمَّتِي إِلَى الغَدَاءِ، وَأَكَلْنَا⁩ ⁧نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي الصَّغِيرَةَ عِنْدَ عَمَّتِي!⁩ … ⁧الكُسْكُسِي. عُدْتُ إِلَى مِيلَانُو سَعِيدَةً، وَلٰكِنْ⁩ 18. Oral production 1. All people. The tutor says a pronoun and a verb (for example, ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ – ⁧قَالَ⁩ »); you answer with the shape ( ⁧قُلْتُنَّ⁩ ). Ten quick exchanges, then inverted roles. 2. Interview with the past. Ask the tutor five questions about his last year using the forms in -ta / -ti; then Tell the third person what he said. 3. My first year (second week). Tell in two minutes your first year of Arabic, without reading, from the section's budget 10. The tutor evaluates Accuracy and Fluidity (heading 6.3) and record the results in the register. 19. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧قَالْتُ⁩ , qāltu ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ : in front of a suffix in consonant the base is short ⁧قَالَنَ⁩ for their own (f.) they have said: ⁧قُلْنَ⁩ : also -na begins with a consonant ⁧مَشُوا⁩ , mašū ⁧مَشَوْا⁩ mašaw: defects in -ā do -aw ⁧نَسِيتُنَسَيْتُ⁩ ⁧نَسِيتُنَسَيْتُ⁩ : the type ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ ago -ītu ⁧دَعَوْتُدَعَيْتُ⁩ : root with ⁧و⁩ ⁧دَعَوْتُدَعَيْتُ⁩  (or ⁧خَرَجَ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ ) ⁧الطُّلَّابُ خَرَجُواالطُّلَّابُ خَرَجَ⁩ Darasna per darasnā (us) · darasna (their, women) ǧitu, qaratu ǧiʾtu, qaraʾtu: the hamza is pronounced 20. Flashcard Deck A2, tag A2-02: 31 rumors. For each new verb, the back of the paper shows the shape Add the wrong forms in the verification to your cards. 21. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. Conjugation (8 points). 1. you (m.) have written · 2. They (f.) understood · 3. You two have studied · 4. I said, "I'm sorry. 5. they (m.) walked · 6. you (f.) have forgotten · 7. we came · 8. You saw B · Phrases (6 points). 9. The employees came out at five (verb before). · 10. The two journalists returned from Beirut (subject first). · 11. I lost my keys. · 12. We invited Karīm Dinner. · 13. Did you (m.) answer the question? · 14. We spent a week in Tunis. C · Analysis (4 points). Indicates person and root: 15. ⁧خِفْتُمْ⁩ · 16. ⁧دَعَوْا⁩ · 17. ⁧بَاعَتَا⁩ · 18. ⁧رَدَدْتُ⁩ D · News (2 points). Translate: 19. ⁧وَقَدْ وَصَلَ الوَفْدُ المِصْرِيُّ إِلَى مِيلَانُو⁩ . · 20. ⁧قَالَ الوَزِيرَانِ إِنَّ الاِجْتِمَاعَ كَانَ مُهِمًّا⁩ . 22. To switch to the next unit Steps to A2-03 if you have at least 16/20 and if in section A you haven't made more mistakes than one form. If the mistakes are on the concave and the defects, do the exercises again 4, 5 and 11 and repeat with the tutor the rapid exchange of oral production 1. The section's budget 10 must be written in the log before starting the form: it is the point of departure on which you will measure the year 2.

title: The complete indicative imperfection
text: Lesson overview The imperfect ( ⁧المُضَارِع⁩ ) is the time of habits, actions in progress and descriptions: "What do you usually do" , "What happens now , but also the headlines at present. In A1 You used it with regular verbs. Here you complete the picture: all people with duals, the prefix in u-, verbs with hamza and, above all, weak verbs, who change to the imperfect more than perfect. The rule of the two bases of A2-02 It's worth it here too. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-03 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites A2-02 exceeded; First year's balance sheet in the register Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 53–54 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-03), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. conjugate to the imperfect a regular verb in all persons, including duals and 'voi / their females; 2. choose the ya- or yu- prefix according to the verb type; 3. combine verbs with hamza ( ⁧يَأْخُذُ⁩ , ⁧يَقْرَأُ⁩ ) and those with ⁧و⁩ initial ( ⁧يَصِلُ⁩ , ⁧يَجِدُ⁩ , ⁧يَضَعُ⁩ ); 4. conjugate concave verbs ( ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧يَبِيعُ⁩ , ⁧يَنَامُ⁩ ) and defects ( ⁧يَمْشِي⁩ , ⁧يَدْعُو⁩ , ⁧يَنْسَى⁩ ), plus ⁧يَأْتِي⁩ and ⁧يَرَى⁩ ; 5. use the imperfect for habits, ongoing actions and nearby programs, with frequency adverbs; 6. understand newspaper titles without vowels built with the imperfect; 7. describe your day and week in 100 words and voice for two minutes. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: all persons · exercise 1 2 Section 2: ya- o yu- · exercise 2 3 Section 3: hamza e ⁧و⁩ initial · year 3 4 Vocabulary (first half) · reading 1 · year 11 5 Section 4: concave · exercise 4 6 Pronunciation · script A and C 7 Review · Anki · describe your day by voice 8 Section 5: defective, ⁧يَأْتِي⁩ , ⁧يَرَى⁩ · year 5 9 Section 6: double verbs · exercise 6 10 Section 7: the uses of the imperfect · exercises 7–8 11 Section 8: titles without vowels · reading 2 · financial years 9 and 12 12 Script B · exercise 10 · writing 13 Session with the tutor: my week Day Activity 14 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · What do you usually do? At the police station, in front of the coffee machine. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ يَا سَارَة! هَلْ تَشْرَبِينَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧قَهْوَةً؟⁩ Lūkā: ṣabāḥu l-ḫayri yā Sāra! hal tašrabīna qahwa? Good morning. Sāra! Do you want a coffee? ⁧لَا، شُكْرًا. أَنَا لَا أَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ أَبَدًا،⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ فَقَطْ.⁩ Sāra: lā, šukran. anā lā ašrabu l- qahwata abadan, ašrabu š-šāya faqaṭ. Sāra: No, thank you. I don't drink coffee, I just drink tea. ⁧مَتَى تَسْتَيْقِظِينَ عَادَةً؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: matā tastayqiẓīna ʿādatan? Luca: What time do you usually wake up? ⁧أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّادِسَةِ، وَأَمْشِي نِصْفَ⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧سَاعَةٍ قَبْلَ العَمَلِ. ثُمَّ أَرْكَبُ المِتْرُو، وَأَصِلُ⁩ ⁧إِلَى المَكْتَبِ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ.⁩ Sāra: astayqiẓu fī s-sādisa, wa-amšī niṣfa sāʿatin qabla l-ʿamal. ṯumma arkabu l-mitrū, wa-aṣilu ilā l-maktabi fī ṯ-ṯāmina. Sāra: I wake up at six and walk half an hour before work. Then I take the subway and get to the office at 8:00. ⁧وَمَاذَا تَفْعَلِينَ فِي المَكْتَبِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-māḏā tafʿalīna fī l-maktab? What are you doing in the office? ⁧أُتَرْجِمُ الرَّسَائِلَ وَالتَّقَارِيرَ، وَأُرَاجِعُ⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧تَرْجَمَاتِ الزُّمَلَاءِ، وَأَحْيَانًا أَتَّصِلُ⁩ ⁧بِالقُنْصُلِيَّاتِ.⁩ Sāra: utarǧimu r-rasāʾila wa-t-taqārīr, wa-urāǧiʿu tarǧamāti z-zumalāʾ, wa- aḥyānan attaṣilu bi-l-qunṣuliyyāt. Sāra: I translate letters and reports, I review the translations of colleagues and sometimes I phone the consulates. ⁧وَكَرِيم وَهُدَى؟ هَلْ يَعْمَلَانِ مَعَكِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-Karīm wa-Hudā? hal yaʿmalāni maʿaki? Luca: And Karīm and Hudā? They work with you? ⁧نَعَمْ، يَعْمَلَانِ فِي المَكْتَبِ نَفْسِهِ. لٰكِنَّ⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧هُدَى تَأْتِي مُتَأَخِّرَةً هٰذَا الأُسْبُوعَ، لِأَنَّ عِنْدَهَا⁩ ⁧نَوْبَةً لَيْلِيَّةً.⁩ Sāra: naʿam, yaʿmalāni fī l-maktabi nafsih. lākinna Hudā taʾtī mutaʾaḫḫiratan hāḏā l-usbūʿ, li-anna ʿindahā nawbatan layliyya. Sāra: Yes, they work in the same office. But Hudā She's late this week, because she has a night shift. ⁧وَمَتَى تَنَامُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-matā tanām? When does he sleep? ⁧تَنَامُ فِي النَّهَارِ، وَتَعُودُ إِلَى العَمَلِ فِي⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧العَاشِرَةِ لَيْلًا. أَنَا لَا أُحِبُّ هٰذِهِ النَّوْبَاتِ!⁩ Sāra: tanāmu fī n-nahār, wa-taʿūdu ilā l-ʿamali fī l-ʿāširati laylan. anā lā uḥibbu hāḏihi n-nawbāt! Sāra: He sleeps during the day and returns to work at 10 p.m. I don't like these shifts! What to notice. ⁧تَشْرَبِينَ⁩ , ⁧تَسْتَيْقِظِينَ⁩ , ⁧تَفْعَلِينَ⁩ : with a woman \"tu" has the suffix -īna. ⁧يَعْمَلَانِ⁩ The two of them work is a dual. Forms with the prefix u- ( ⁧أُتَرْجِمُ⁩ , ⁧أُرَاجِعُ⁩ , ⁧أُحِبُّ⁩ ) belong to verbs of a different type than simple ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ : you see it in the section 2. ⁧تَأْتِي⁩ It comes, arrives, and ⁧تَعُودُ⁩ Torna are weak verbs, ⁧أَصِلُ⁩ has lost the ⁧و⁩ root ( ⁧و ص ل⁩ ). ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧أَبَدًا⁩ it means "never..." never "never." 2. The imperfect in all people The imperfect prefixes (in all people) and, in some people, suffixes. Conjugation complete of ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ : Person Proname Form Transliteration me  ⁧أَدْرُسُأَنَا⁩ adrusu you (m.)  ⁧تَدْرُسُأَنْتَ⁩ tadrusu you (f.)  ⁧تَدْرُسِينَأَنْتِ⁩ tadrusīna him  ⁧يَدْرُسُهُوَ⁩ yadrusu She  ⁧تَدْرُسُهِيَ⁩ tadrusu You two.  ⁧تَدْرُسَانِأَنْتُمَا⁩ tadrusāni the two of them (m.)  ⁧يَدْرُسَانِهُمَا⁩ yadrusāni The two of them (f.)  ⁧تَدْرُسَانِهُمَا⁩ tadrusāni us  ⁧نَدْرُسُنَحْنُ⁩ nadrusu you (m.)  ⁧تَدْرُسُونَأَنْتُمْ⁩ tadrusūna vol (f.)  ⁧تَدْرُسْنَأَنْتُنَّ⁩ tadrusna They (m.)  ⁧يَدْرُسُونَهُمْ⁩ yadrusūna They (f.) ⁧يَدْرُسْنَهُنَّ⁩ yadrusna Three comments you need for the entire form. 1. The prefix ta- has five uses (you m., she, you two, them two f., you): without context ⁧تَدْرُسُ⁩ may be studies or studies. In the texts it decides the subject expressed or the context. 2. The -u terminations, -īna, -āni, -ūna are the sign of the sign. In conjunction (A2-04) and in the jurissive (A2-05) will change: the -u becomes -a or disappears, and the -na / -ni final falls. Learn how to see these endings as a piece apart: tadrus- īna , yadrus- āni , yadrus- ūna . 3. -na of .../they (f.) is not a termination of the indication: it is the sign of the female plural, and remains in all the ways. In front of -na the base has no final vowel (yadrus-na): like the perfect, it is a suffix that begins with a consonant. In pause the final -u falls (adrus, yadrus); terminations -īna, -āni, -ūna are pronounced -īn, -ān, -ūn. 3. The prefix: ya- or yu-? Prefix Type of verb Examples ya-, ta-, a-, na- simple verb (form I) and forms with t- or st- before root (V, VI, VII, VIII, X) ⁧يَسْتَيْقِظُ⁩ , ⁧يَنْتَظِرُ⁩ , ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ yu-, you-, u-, nu- forms II, III, IV and verbs of four consonants ⁧يُدَرِّسُ⁩ (II), ⁧يُسَاعِدُ⁩ (III), ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ (IV), ⁧يُتَرْجِمُ⁩ The prefix in u- always goes along with one i before the last root consonant: yu-darr i su, yu-sā ʿi du, yu- tar ǧi mu. The derived forms you will study one by one A2-17 and A2-18; for now learn to recognize the prefix, because it distinguishes different verbs of the same root: • ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ yadrusu ... ⁧يُدَرِّسُ⁩ yudarrisu • ⁧يَعْلَمُ⁩ yaʿlamu "Sa" is "sa" ⁧يُعَلِّمُ⁩ yuʿallimu Instruction, instruction and training 4. Verbs with hamza and verbs with ⁧و⁩ initial With hamza. They're regular. Two particularities: • Verbs starting with hamza: two hamzees in a row merge into ā long written ⁧آ⁩ : ⁧أَأْخُذُ⁩ → ⁧آخُذُ⁩ āḫuḏu, ⁧أَأْكُلُ⁩ → ⁧آكُلُ⁩ ākulu; • the hamza changes support in front of -īna and -ūna: ⁧تَقْرَئِينَ⁩ taqraʾīna, ⁧يَقْرَؤُونَ⁩ yaqraʾūna (also ⁧يَقْرَأُونَ⁩ ). The rules are in A2-16. With ⁧و⁩ initial (verbs .) (assimilated) In form I ⁧و⁩ of the root disappears to the imperfect. It is a regular loss: all people have the basis without ⁧و⁩ . Perfect Imperfect me They (m.) ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ • arriving • ⁧يَصِلُ⁩ yaṣilu  ⁧يَصِلُونَأَصِلُ⁩ ⁧وَجَدَ⁩ • find • • ⁧يَجِدُ⁩ yaǧidu  ⁧يَجِدُونَأَجِدُ⁩ ⁧وَقَفَ⁩ • Stop • • ⁧يَقِفُ⁩ yaqifu  ⁧يَقِفُونَأَقِفُ⁩ ⁧وَضَعَ⁩ • Put it on • ⁧يَضَعُ⁩ yaḍaʿu  ⁧يَضَعُونَأَضَعُ⁩ ⁧وَقَعَ⁩ • fall; to be found ⁧يَقَعُ⁩ yaqaʿu ⁧يَقَعُونَأَقَعُ⁩ How do you recognize it in a text: a word like ⁧يصل⁩ seems to have a root of two letters ( ⁧ص ل⁩ ). If you don't find anything in the dictionary with two letters, try one ⁧و⁩ front: ⁧و ص ل⁩ . In derived forms the ⁧و⁩ may remain or assimilate: ⁧يَتَّصِلُ⁩ Call, contact ⁧و ص ل⁩ ( ⁧و⁩ has become ⁧ت⁩ And it doubled: A2-18). 5. Concave verbs to the imperfect The concave has a long vowel in the center: ū, ī or ā. It is the same vowel that determines the short vowel of the perfect (A2-02Section 5). Type Examples Perfect ū , ⁧يَزُورُ⁩ , ⁧يَكُونُ⁩ , ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ ⁧قُلْتُيَعُودُ⁩ ⁧عُدْتُ⁩ , ⁧زُرْتُ⁩ , ⁧كُنْتُ⁩ , ī , ⁧يَبِيعُ⁩ ⁧بِعْتُيَعِيشُ⁩ ⁧عِشْتُ⁩ , ā ⁧نِمْتُيَخَافُ⁩ , ⁧يَنَامُ⁩ ⁧خِفْتُ⁩ , The rule of the two bases, to the imperfect. The long vowel remains in almost all people, because almost all suffixes begin with a vowel. The exception is -na of 'voi / loro (f.) Person  ⁧يَنَامُيَبِيعُيَقُولُ⁩  me  ⁧أَنَامُأَبِيعُأَقُولُ⁩  you (f.)  ⁧تَنَامِينَتَبِيعِينَتَقُولِينَ⁩  him  ⁧يَنَامُيَبِيعُيَقُولُ⁩  The two of them  ⁧يَنَامَانِيَبِيعَانِيَقُولَانِ⁩  us  ⁧نَنَامُنَبِيعُنَقُولُ⁩  you (m.)  ⁧تَنَامُونَتَبِيعُونَتَقُولُونَ⁩  vol (f.) ⁧تَقُلْنَ⁩ taqulna ⁧تَبِعْنَ⁩ tabiʿna ⁧تَنَمْنَ⁩ tanamna They (m.)  ⁧يَنَامُونَيَبِيعُونَيَقُولُونَ⁩  They (f.) ⁧يَقُلْنَ⁩ yaqulna ⁧يَبِعْنَ⁩ yabiʿna ⁧يَنَمْنَ⁩ yanamna The short forms of "voi" / their (f.) are rare in the texts, but the same reduction will return, much more frequent, to the juxtaposition: ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ ( A2-05). 6. Who are we talking about? ⁧١. أُدَرِّسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ.⁩ ⁧٢. أَدْرُسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ.⁩ ⁧٣. هَلْ تَمْشِينَ إِلَى العَمَلِ؟⁩ ⁧٤. هُمْ يَنْسَوْنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ!⁩ ⁧٥. نَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى العَشَاءِ.⁩ ⁧٦. أَنْتُمْ لَا تَرَوْنَ المُشْكِلَةَ.⁩ ⁧٧. هُمَا يَصِلَانِ غَدًا.⁩ ⁧٨. آخُذُ الحَافِلَةَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.⁩ ! ⁧دَائِمًا⁩ « ⁧لَا⁩ » ⁧٩. هُنَّ يَقُلْنَ⁩ ⁧١٠. لِمَاذَا تَتَأَخَّرِينَ؟⁩ Script C · The day of Sāra ⁧اِسْمِي سَارَة، وَأَنَا مُتَرْجِمَةٌ لُبْنَانِيَّةٌ. أَسْكُنُ فِي مِيلَانُو مُنْذُ ثَلَاثِ سَنَوَاتٍ. أَسْتَيْقِظُ عَادَةً فِي السَّادِسَةِ،⁩ ⁧وَلَا أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مُنَبِّهٍ. أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ وَأَقْرَأُ الأَخْبَارَ اللُّبْنَانِيَّةَ عَلَى الهَاتِفِ. فِي العَمَلِ أُتَرْجِمُ وَأُرَاجِعُ،⁩ ⁧وَأَحْيَانًا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَحْكَمَةِ مَعَ الزُّمَلَاءِ. لَا آكُلُ فِي المَكْتَبِ أَبَدًا: نَخْرُجُ أَنَا وَهُدَى إِلَى مَطْعَمٍ صَغِيرٍ⁩ ⁧قَرِيبٍ. فِي المَسَاءِ أَتَّصِلُ بِأُمِّي فِي بَيْرُوتَ، وَيَوْمَ السَّبْتِ أَرْتَاحُ: لَا أَعْمَلُ وَلَا أُتَرْجِمُ!⁩ 17. Oral production 1. My day. Tell the tutor a day of your own in a minute, then answer three questions with frequency adverbs ( ⁧مَتَى⁩ … ⁧؟ كَمْ مَرَّةً⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ How many times...? 2. Interview. Ask the tutor what he usually does on the weekend; then refer to the third person ( ⁧يَسْتَيْقِظُ⁩ …, ⁧يَذْهَبُ⁩ …). 3. My week (second week). title: The future withسَـ‎ e ‎سَوْفَ‎ · ‎لَنْand the conjunctive
text: Lesson overview In this unit you learn to talk about projects: what you will do, what you will not do, what you want, must and can do. The future is simple, just a prefix; the real grammatical novelty is the conjunctiva ( ⁧المَنْصُوب⁩ ), the manner of the verb that follows ⁧أَنْ⁩ . ⁧لَنْ⁩ Not (in the future) and particles of purpose. In Arabic, the conjunctive expresses no doubt, as in English: it is an obligatory form after certain words. From here also the story of this level: Salmā invites Luke and Mary to Cairo for the summer. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-04 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites A2-03 exceeded (imperfect table, weak verbs included) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 55–56 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-04), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week (accept and refuse) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. Talking about the future with ⁧سَـ⁩ and ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ and deny it with ⁧لَنْ⁩ ; 2. form the conjunctiva of all studied verbs, including the weak; 3. use ⁧أَنْ⁩ + conjunctive after "volare" , "power" , "duty" , "test" , "meaning" , "intention" , "power" , "must" , "test" , "test" , "intention" , "intention" 4. use ⁧يَجِبُ أَنْ⁩ and ⁧يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ with the right person; 5. to express the purpose with ⁧لِـ⁩ , ⁧لِكَيْ⁩ , ⁧كَيْ⁩ and ⁧حَتَّى⁩ ; 6. to accept and refuse an invitation, in writing and in writing, with the appropriate formulas; 7. understand an invitation email and write a reply to 90 words. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · What are you doing in July? After class, Salmā He stops to talk to Luca. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧لُوكَا، مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ فِي الصَّيْفِ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Lūkā, māḏā sa-tafʿalu fī ṣ-ṣayf? Salmā: Luca, what are you going to do in the summer? ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ بَعْدُ. رُبَّمَا سَأَبْقَى فِي مِيلَانُو.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧لِمَاذَا؟⁩ Lūkā: lā aʿrifu baʿd. rubbamā sa-abqā fī Mīlānū. li-māḏā? I don't know yet. Maybe I'll stay in Milan. Why? ⁧سَأُسَافِرُ إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ فِي يُولْيُو،⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧وَعِنْدِي فِكْرَةٌ: هُنَاكَ دَوْرَةٌ مُكَثَّفَةٌ لِلْأَجَانِبِ⁩ ⁧فِي مَرْكَزِ لُغَاتٍ.⁩ Salmā: sa-usāfiru ilā l-Qāhirati fī yūlyū, wa-ʿindī fikra: hunāka dawratun mukaṯṯafatun li-l-aǧānibi fī markazi luġāt. Salmā: In July I will go to Cairo, and I have an idea: there is an intensive course for foreigners in a language center. ⁧فِكْرَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ! كَمْ أُسْبُوعًا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: fikratun ǧamīla! kam usbūʿan? Good idea! How many weeks? ⁧أُسْبُوعَانِ. يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَدْرُسَ فِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧الصَّبَاحِ، وَفِي المَسَاءِ سَنَزُورُ المَدِينَةَ.⁩ Salmā: usbūʿān. yumkinuka an tadrusa fī ṣ-ṣabāḥ, wa-fī l-masāʾi sa-nazūru l- madīna. SalmāTwo weeks. You can study in the morning, and in the evening we will visit the city. ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ آتِيَ، بِكُلِّ سُرُورٍ! لٰكِنْ يَجِبُ أَنْ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧أَطْلُبَ إِجَازَةً مِنَ العَمَلِ.⁩ Lūkā: urīdu an ātiya, bi-kulli surūr! lākin yaǧibu an aṭluba iǧāzatan mina l- ʿamal. Luca: I want to come, with great pleasure! But I have to ask for vacation at work. ⁧طَبْعًا. وَمَارْيَا؟ هَلْ سَتَأْتِي؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: ṭabʿan. wa-Māryā? hal sa-taʾtī? Salmā: Sure. What about Maria? Will he come? ⁧لَا أَظُنُّ. قَالَتْ لِي إِنَّهَا لَنْ تَأْخُذَ إِجَازَةً⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧فِي يُولْيُو.⁩ Lūkā: lā aẓunn. qālat lī innahā lan taʾḫuḏa iǧāzatan fī yūlyū. I don't think so. He told me he won't take vacation in July. Salmā: sa-aktubu lakumā risālatani l- Salmā: Tonight I write you a ⁧سَأَكْتُبُ لَكُمَا رِسَالَةً اللَّيْلَةَ، فِيهَا كُلُّ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Laylata, fīhā kullu l-maʿlūmāt. message with all the information. ⁧المَعْلُومَاتِ.⁩ What to notice. ⁧سَتَفْعَلُ⁩ , ⁧سَأَبْقَى⁩ , ⁧سَنَزُورُ⁩ : the future is the imperfect with ⁧سَـ⁩ Attacked. ⁧بَعْدُ⁩ (a) u) after a denial it means "still": ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ بَعْدُ⁩ I don't know yet. After ⁧أَنْ⁩ and ⁧لَنْ⁩ the verb ends in -a: ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسَ⁩ , ⁧أَنْ أَطْلُبَ⁩ , ⁧لَنْ تَأْخُذَ⁩ ; ⁧أَنْ آتِيَ⁩ is the conjunctive of ⁧آتِي. يُمْكِنُكَ⁩ You can: who can be indicated by the suffix pronoun. ⁧لَا أَظُنُّ⁩ I don't think it comes from ⁧ظَنَّ⁩ A double verb (A2-16). ⁧قَالَتْ⁩ … ⁧إِنَّهَا⁩ You said that you... ......................................................................................................................................................................................... ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ( A2-19). ⁧كَمْ أُسْبُوعًا⁩ : after ⁧كَمْ⁩ the name is singularly accusative (A1-06). ⁧لَكُمَا⁩ You two are. 2. The future: ⁧سَـ⁩ and ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ The future is formed by putting ⁧سَـ⁩ (a) or ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ (sawfa) in front of the imperfect indicative . The verb doesn't change. Present Future with ⁧سَـ⁩ Future with ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ Translation  ⁧سَوْفَ أُسَافِرُسَأُسَافِرُأُسَافِرُ⁩  I'll leave.  ⁧سَوْفَ تَأْتِينَسَتَأْتِينَتَأْتِينَ⁩  you will come (f.)  ⁧سَوْفَ يَكُونُسَيَكُونُيَكُونُ⁩  will be  ⁧سَوْفَ نَزُورُسَنَزُورُنَزُورُ⁩ ⁧سَوْفَ نَزُورُسَنَزُورُنَزُورُ⁩ we'll visit ⁧سَوْفَ يَدْعُونَسَيَدْعُونَيَدْعُونَ⁩ invite Difference in use. The meaning is the same. ⁧سَـ⁩ is more frequent and neutral; ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ is more formal, hears itself in speeches and often indicates a future farther or more decisive. In newspaper headlines, you often find only the imperfect (A2-03) with value of near future. Spelling. ⁧سَـ⁩ writes attached to the verb and leaves no room: ⁧سَأَكْتُبُ⁩ , not * ⁧سَ أَكْتُبُ⁩ . ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ It's a separate word. Neither one attaches itself to other parts of the speech: the future is not used with nominal phrases, which have no verb. The future of ⁧كَانَ⁩ : ⁧سَيَكُونُ الاِجْتِمَاعُ طَوِيلًا⁩ The meeting will be long, with the predicate to the accusative as after ⁧كَانَ⁩ ( A1-18). ⁧إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ . In Arabic use, a future project is often accompanied by this formula, even among non-religious people: ⁧سَأَرَاكَ غَدًا، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ See you tomorrow, if God wills. It's courtesy, not uncertainty; But beware of the tone: in certain contexts it can also be a kind way not to engage. 3. The denial of the future: ⁧لَنْ⁩ The future is not denied by ⁧لَا⁩ . Use ⁧لَنْ⁩ + conjunctive , without ⁧سَـ⁩ and without ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ : Affirmative Negative Translation ⁧سَأَذْهَبُ.⁩ ⁧لَنْ أَذْهَبَ.⁩ I'm not going. ⁧سَتَتَأَخَّرِينَ.⁩ ⁧لَنْ تَتَأَخَّرِي.⁩ You won't be late (f.). ⁧سَيَأْتُونَ.⁩ ⁧لَنْ يَأْتُوا.⁩ They're not coming. ⁧لَنْ⁩ It's a strong negation: "I won't... (and I won't) " Many Arabic speakers deny the future with dialectal forms in their daily speech; in the written and formal standard the correct form is always ⁧لَنْ⁩ . 4. The conjunctive ( ⁧المَنْصُوب⁩ ) The conjunctive is obtained from the indicative imperfection with two changes, which you have already seen announced in A2-03 (section 2): 1. the final -u becomes -a: ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ → ⁧يَدْرُسَ⁩ ; 2. terminations -īna, -āni, -ūna I forgive the -na / -ni: ⁧تَدْرُسِينَ⁩ → ⁧تَدْرُسِي⁩ , ⁧يَدْرُسَانِ⁩ → ⁧يَدْرُسَا⁩ , ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ → ⁧يَدْرُسُوا⁩ (with the breathless, like the perfect). The -na of the female plural ( ⁧تَدْرُسْنَ⁩ , ⁧يَدْرُسْنَ⁩ ) does not fall: it is not a termination of the indication. Person Indicative Joint (after ⁧أَنْ⁩ ) me  ⁧أَنْ أَدْرُسَأَدْرُسُ⁩ you (m.)  ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسَتَدْرُسُ⁩ you (f.)  ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسِيتَدْرُسِينَ⁩ he · she · ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسَتَدْرُسُ⁩ ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسَ⁩ · you two · the two of them ⁧يَدْرُسَانِ⁩ · ⁧تَدْرُسَانِ⁩ ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسَا⁩ · ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسَا⁩ us  ⁧أَنْ نَدْرُسَنَدْرُسُ⁩ you (m.) ⁧تَدْرُسُونَ⁩ ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسُوا⁩ vol (f.)  ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسْنَتَدْرُسْنَ⁩ They (m.) ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسُوا⁩ They (f.)  ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسْنَيَدْرُسْنَ⁩ In pause the -a final falls, like the -u: ⁧لَنْ أَذْهَبَ⁩ read Ian aḏhab. For this reason the difference between indicative and conjunctive is felt mainly in the five people who lose the -na: tadrusīn / tadrusī, yadrusūn / yadrusū. title: The past denied byلَمْand the juxtant
text: Lesson overview In A1-18 you denied the past with ⁧مَا⁩ + perfect and you recognized ⁧لَمْ⁩ . In the written language, in the news and in the reports, the normal denial of the past is precisely ⁧لَمْ⁩ + ⁧المَجْزُوم⁩ ): ⁧لَمْ يَحْضُرِ الوَزِيرُ⁩ The Minister did not attend the meeting, ⁧لَمْ تَقَعْ إِصَابَاتٌ⁩ There were no injuries. The juxtaposed is the third way of the imperfect: after the indicative (A2-03) and the conjunctive (A2-04), here the final vowel disappears completely, and in the weak verbs also shortens the internal vowel. It's the unit that really makes you read the news. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-05 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites A2-04 out-of-date (joint, including weak) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 57–58 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-05), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to form the juxtaposition of the regular verbs in all persons; 2. deny the past with ⁧لَمْ⁩ , even with weak verbs ( ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَأْتِ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَنْسَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَرَ⁩ ); 3. choose between ⁧مَا⁩ + perfect and ⁧لَمْ⁩ + negative according to the register; 4. use ⁧لَمْ⁩ … ⁧بَعْدُ⁩ Not... yet. ⁧لَمْ يَعُدْ⁩ Not... more... ⁧لَمَّا⁩ ; 5. understand short news and a report of teaching service full of denials; 6. tell a mishap and write a short report of 100 words. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · A wrong day Karīm He arrives at the office at 10:00. Hudā He's waiting for me. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧كَرِيم! أَخِيرًا! لِمَاذَا لَمْ تَأْتِ إِلَى⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧الاِجْتِمَاعِ؟⁩ Hudā: Karīm! aḫīran! li-māḏā lam taʾti ilā l-iǧtimāʿ? Hudā: Karīm! Finally! Why didn't you come to the meeting? ⁧لَا تَسْأَلِي! هٰذَا الصَّبَاحُ لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧صَبَاحِي.⁩ Karīm: lā tasʾalī! hāḏā ṣ-ṣabāḥu lam yakun ṣabāḥī. Karīm: Don't ask me! This morning wasn't my morning. ⁧مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: māḏā ḥadaṯ? Hudā: What happened? ⁧أَوَّلًا لَمْ أَسْمَعِ المُنَبِّهَ. ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧بِسُرْعَةٍ، وَالسَّيَّارَةُ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ.⁩ Karīm: awwalan lam asmaʿi l- munabbih. ṯumma ḫaraǧtu bi-surʿa, wa-s-sayyāratu lam taʿmal. Karīm: I didn't hear the alarm before. Then I ran out, and the car didn't start. ⁧وَلِمَاذَا لَمْ تَرْكَبِ الحَافِلَةَ؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: wa-li-māḏā lam tarkabi l-ḥāfila? Hudā: Why didn't you take the bus? ⁧اِنْتَظَرْتُ عِشْرِينَ دَقِيقَةً، وَلَمْ تَأْتِ!⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧وَلَمْ أَجِدْ هَاتِفِي لِكَيْ أَتَّصِلَ بِكُمْ.⁩ Karīm: intaẓartu ʿišrīna daqīqa, wa-lam taʾti! wa-lam aǧid hātifī li-kay attaṣila bikum. Karīm: I waited twenty minutes and did not arrive! And I didn't find the phone to call you. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ. الاِجْتِمَاعُ لَمْ يَكُنْ طَوِيلًا،⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧وَالمُدِيرُ لَمْ يَقُلْ شَيْئًا مُهِمًّا.⁩ Hudā: lā baʾs. al-iǧtimāʿu lam yakun ṭawīlan, wa-l-mudīru lam yaqul šayʾan muhimman. Hudā: It's okay. The meeting wasn't long, and the director didn't say anything important. ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ! وَهَلْ وَصَلَتْ تَرْجَمَةُ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧التَّقْرِيرِ؟⁩ Karīm: al-ḥamdu li-llāh! wa-hal waṣalat tarǧamatu t-taqrīr? Karīm: Thank goodness! And the translation of the report has arrived? Hudā: lā, lam taṣil baʿd. Sāra lam Hudā: No, it has not arrived yet. ⁧لَا، لَمْ تَصِلْ بَعْدُ. سَارَة لَمْ تَنْتَهِ مِنْهَا.⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ so muchhi minhā. Sāra He didn't finish it. What to notice. After ⁧لَمْ⁩ the verb loses the final vowel: ⁧لَمْ تَعْمَلْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ أَجِدْ⁩ . In weak verbs the internal vowel is also shortened: ⁧يَكُونُ⁩ → ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ , ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ → ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ , ⁧تَأْتِي⁩ → ⁧لَمْ تَأْتِ⁩ , ⁧تَنْتَهِي⁩ → ⁧لَمْ تَنْتَهِ⁩ . In front of the article sukūn becomes i: ⁧لَمْ أَسْمَعِ المُنَبِّهَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ تَرْكَبِ الحَافِلَةَ. لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ , as ⁧كَانَ⁩ , wants the predicate to the accusative: ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ طَوِيلًا. لَا تَسْأَلِي⁩ Do not ask!It is a prohibition: ⁧لَا⁩ +A2-06). ⁧بِسُرْعَةٍ⁩ Quickly, quickly. ⁧شَيْئًا مُهِمًّا⁩ : after a denial ⁧شَيْء⁩ it means "nothing" is "nothing." 2. The Jurissive ( ⁧المَجْزُوم⁩ ) e ⁧لَمْ⁩ The juxtaposition is obtained from the imperfect indicative with two changes: 1. the final -u disappears and the consonant remains with the sukūn: ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ → ⁧يَدْرُسْ⁩ ; 2. terminations -īna, -āni, -ūna They lose the -na / -ni , just like in the conjunctive: ⁧تَدْرُسِي⁩ , ⁧يَدْرُسَا⁩ , ⁧يَدْرُسُوا⁩ . The -na of the female plural remains: ⁧يَدْرُسْنَ⁩ . Person Indicative Joint Judging (after ⁧لَمْ⁩ ) me   ⁧لَمْ أَدْرُسْأَنْ أَدْرُسَأَدْرُسُ⁩ you (m.)   ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسْأَنْ تَدْرُسَتَدْرُسُ⁩ you (f.)   ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسِيأَنْ تَدْرُسِيتَدْرُسِينَ⁩ he · she · ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ ⁧لَمْ يَدْرُسْأَنْ يَدْرُسَتَدْرُسُ⁩ ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسْ⁩ · you two · the two of them ⁧يَدْرُسَانِ⁩ · ⁧تَدْرُسَانِ⁩ ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسَا⁩ ⁧لَمْ يَدْرُسَا⁩ · ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسَا⁩ us   ⁧لَمْ نَدْرُسْأَنْ نَدْرُسَنَدْرُسُ⁩ you (m. · f.) ⁧تَدْرُسْنَ⁩ · ⁧تَدْرُسُونَ⁩ ⁧أَنْ تَدْرُسُوا⁩ ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسْنَ⁩ · ⁧لَمْ تَدْرُسُوا⁩ They (m. · f.) ⁧يَدْرُسْنَ⁩ · ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ ⁧أَنْ يَدْرُسُوا⁩ ⁧لَمْ يَدْرُسْنَ⁩ · ⁧لَمْ يَدْرُسُوا⁩ The key point. ⁧لَمْ⁩ + juxive has past value, even if the form is that of the imperfect: ⁧لَمْ يَدْرُسْ⁩ It has not been studied, not studied. Time is in ⁧لَمْ⁩ Not in the verb. The support vowel. One sukūn followed by an alif waṣla (Article, ⁧اِسْم⁩ , ⁧اِبْن⁩ ...) takes one i: ⁧لَمْ يَحْضُرِ الوَزِيرُ⁩ (lam yaḥḍuri l-wazīr), ⁧لَمْ أَسْمَعِ الخَبَرَ⁩ . In texts without vowels, the regular juxtaposition is written as the indicative ( ⁧لم يدرس⁩ ): you recognize it from ⁧لَمْ⁩ . It is seen instead in the weak ( ⁧لم يكن⁩ , ⁧لم يأت⁩ , ⁧لم ير⁩ ) and in the forms that lose the ⁧ن⁩ ( ⁧لم يدرسوا⁩ ). 3. ⁧مَا⁩ or ⁧لَمْ⁩ ? The meaning is the same, ... I don't have / isn't... title: The imperative and the prohibition
text: Lesson overview The imperative ( ⁧الأَمْر⁩ ) is used to give instructions, advice and orders; the ban to say what not to do. These are the forms of signs, instructions at the airport, forms and, for a policeman, many service phrases (sit down) , ... complete this form , ... don't touch it). They are all built on the juxtaposition of A2-05: if you can say ⁧لَمْ تَكْتُبْ⁩ , you can already say "write!" and "don't write!" A week. Item Details Code A2-06 Level A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system Prerequisites A2-05 exceeded (legal, including weak) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 59 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-06), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form the imperative of a regular verb in all people (m., f., dual, plural m. e f.); 2. Choose the supporting vowel ( ⁧اُ⁩ or ⁧اِ⁩ ) and recognize the imperative of form IV with ⁧أَ⁩ ; 3. to form the imperative of the most frequent weak verbs and irregular verbs ( ⁧قُلْ⁩ , ⁧ضَعْ⁩ , ⁧خُذْ⁩ , ⁧كُلْ⁩ , ⁧تَعَالَ⁩ …); 4. to make a ban with ⁧لَا⁩ + Judging; 5. Make a request more kind and recognize the impersonal forms of cartels ( ⁧مَمْنُوع⁩ , ⁧الرَّجَاءُ⁩ , ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ ); 6. give and request simple instructions in voice and in writing. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · sections 1–2: the regular imperative · exercises 1–2 2 Section 3: weak and irregular verbs · exercise 3 · vocabulary 3 Section 4: the prohibition · section 5: courtesy and signs · exercises 4–6 4 Reading 1 and 2 · financial years 9–10 5 Listening (script B and C) · Exercises 7–8 · writing 6 Session with the tutor: give and ask for instructions 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · At the door A man walks into the police station. Hudā He's at the door. Arabic Transliteration Translation ar-raǧul: masāʾu l-ḫayr. Faqadtu Man: Good evening. I lost the ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ. فَقَدْتُ جَوَازَ سَفَرِي،⁩ : ⁧الرَّجُلُ⁩ ǧawāza safarī, wa-lā aʿrifu māḏā afʿal. passport and I don't know what to do. ⁧وَلَا أَعْرِفُ مَاذَا أَفْعَلُ.⁩ Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَسَاءُ النُّورِ. تَفَضَّلْ، اِجْلِسْ هُنَا. لَا⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧تَقْلَقْ، سَنُسَاعِدُكَ.⁩ Hudā: masāʾu n-nūr. tafaḍḍal, iǧlis hunā. lā taqlaq, sa-nusāʿiduk. Hudā: Good evening. Please sit here. Don't worry, we'll help you. ⁧شُكْرًا.⁩ : ⁧الرَّجُلُ⁩ ar-raǧul: šukran. The man: Thank you. ⁧خُذْ هٰذِهِ الاِسْتِمَارَةَ. اِمْلَأْهَا، وَاكْتُبِ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧اسْمَكَ بِالحُرُوفِ اللَّاتِينِيَّةِ أَيْضًا.⁩ Hudā: ḫuḏ hāḏihi l-istimāra. imlaʾhā, wa-ktubi smaka bi-l-ḥurūfi l-lātīniyyati ayḍan. Hudā: Take this form. You fill it out, and write his name in Latin characters. ⁧هَلْ أَكْتُبُ رَقْمَ الجَوَازِ؟ لَا أَتَذَكَّرُهُ.⁩ : ⁧الرَّجُلُ⁩ ar-raǧul: hal aktubu raqma l-ǧawāz? lā ataḏakkaruh. The man: Do I have to write the passport number? I don't remember. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ، اُتْرُكْهُ. لٰكِنْ لَا تَنْسَ رَقْمَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧هَاتِفِكَ. ثُمَّ وَقِّعْ هُنَا، فِي الأَسْفَلِ.⁩ Hudā: lā baʾs, utrukhu. lākin lā tansa raqma hātifik. ṯumma waqqiʿ hunā, fī l- asfal. Hudā: It's okay, leave it blank. But don't forget your phone number. Then sign down here. ⁧وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ؟⁩ : ⁧الرَّجُلُ⁩ ar-raǧul: wa-baʿda ḏālik? The Man - And After? ⁧اِنْتَظِرْ قَلِيلًا، وَسَنُعْطِيكَ نُسْخَةً مِنَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧المَحْضَرِ. غَدًا اِذْهَبْ إِلَى القُنْصُلِيَّةِ مَعَ هٰذِهِ⁩ ⁧النُّسْخَةِ وَصُورَتَيْنِ.⁩ Hudā: intaẓir qalīlan, wa-sa-nuʿṭīka nusḫatan mina l-maḥḍar. ġadani ḏhab ilā l-qunṣuliyyati maʿa hāḏihi n-nusḫati wa-ṣūratayn. Hudā: Wait a minute, we'll give you a copy of the report. Go to the consulate tomorrow with this copy and two photos. What to notice. Hudā use the "Tu" ( ⁧اِجْلِسْ⁩ , ⁧خُذْ⁩ , ⁧وَقِّعْ⁩ ): in Arabic, the imperative does not have a kindness such as the Italian "Lei" (Italian); the courtesy passes by the tone, ⁧تَفَضَّلْ⁩ and for formulas (section 5). In the Italian translation we use the "lei" . ⁧اِمْلَأْهَا⁩ , ⁧اُتْرُكْهُ⁩ : the object pronoun attaches itself to the imperative. ⁧وَاكْتُبِ اسْمَكَ⁩ : after ⁧وَ⁩ the support wing is not pronounced (wa-ktubi), and the sukūn Takes one i in front of the alif waṣla of ⁧اِسْم. لَا تَقْلَقْ⁩ - do not worry, and ⁧لَا تَنْسَ⁩ "Do not forget" are prohibitions: ⁧لَا⁩ + Judging. ⁧نُسْخَة⁩ (a) a copy of the certificate; ⁧فِي الأَسْفَلِ⁩ They're in the vocabulary. 2. The imperative of regular verbs The imperative exists only for the second person (you, you). It is formed by the juxtaposed: 1. Take the judge of the second person: ⁧تَكْتُبْ⁩ , ⁧تَكْتُبِي⁩ , ⁧تَكْتُبَا⁩ , ⁧تَكْتُبُوا⁩ , ⁧تَكْتُبْنَ⁩ ; 2. remove the prefix ⁧تَـ⁩ : ⁧كْتُبْ⁩ …; 3. if the word begins with two consonants (k-t-), add an aliif with vowel support: ⁧اُ⁩ if vowel of the root is u , ⁧اِ⁩ if it is a or i . Person ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ ( u) ⁧يَذْهَبُ⁩ ( a) ⁧يَجْلِسُ⁩ ( i) you (m.) ⁧اُكْتُبْ⁩ uktub ⁧اِذْهَبْ⁩ iḏhab ⁧اِجْلِسْ⁩ iǧlis you (f.) ⁧اُكْتُبِي⁩ uktubī ⁧اِذْهَبِي⁩ iḏhabī ⁧اِجْلِسِي⁩ iǧlisī You two. ⁧اُكْتُبَا⁩ uktubā ⁧اِذْهَبَا⁩ iḏhabā ⁧اِجْلِسَا⁩ iǧlisā you (m.) ⁧اُكْتُبُوا⁩ uktubū ⁧اِذْهَبُوا⁩ iḏhabū ⁧اِجْلِسُوا⁩ iǧlisū vol (f.) ⁧اُكْتُبْنَ⁩ uktubna ⁧اِذْهَبْنَ⁩ iḏhabna ⁧اِجْلِسْنَ⁩ iǧlisna The alif of the imperative is an alif waṣla : after a word that ends in vowel, or after ⁧وَ⁩ / ⁧فَ⁩ , the following shall not be pronounced: ⁧وَاكْتُبْ⁩ wa-ktub, ⁧ثُمَّ اذْهَبْ⁩ ṯumma ḏhab. The ban: ⁧لَا⁩ + Judging To say "don't do it": you don't use the imperative: you use ⁧لَا⁩ + second person's rating, with the prefix. Emissary Prohibition Translation  ⁧لَا تَكْتُبْاُكْتُبْ⁩ do not write  ⁧لَا تَجْلِسِياِجْلِسِي⁩ do not sit (f.) ⁧قُولُوا⁩ ⁧لَا تَقُولُوا⁩ do not say  ⁧لَا تَنْسَاِنْسَ⁩ don't forget  ⁧لَا تَأْخُذْخُذْ⁩ do not take  ⁧لَا تَأْتِتَعَالَ⁩ Don't come. ⁧لَا تَتَأَخَّرْتَأَخَّرْ⁩ Don't be late. Attention to comparison with A2-03: ⁧لَا⁩ + indicative is the negation of the present ( ⁧لَا تَكْتُبُ⁩ • do not write • ⁧لَا⁩ + the prohibition is justified ( ⁧لَا تَكْتُبْ⁩ Do not write! In regular verbs the difference is only in the final vowel; In the weak and in the people with suffix you can see well: ⁧لَا تَنْسَى⁩ Do not forget to... ⁧لَا تَنْسَ⁩ Don't forget! ⁧لَا⁩ ⁧تَكْتُبُونَ⁩ / ⁧لَا تَكْتُبُوا⁩ . 5. Courtesy, cartels, instructions Make a request polite. The nude imperative can sound abrupt. It softens with: Formula Example ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ / ⁧فَضْلِكِ⁩ Please. ⁧اِنْتَظِرْ قَلِيلًا مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.⁩ ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ / ⁧سَمَحْتِ⁩ If you allow me, please. ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، أَغْلِقِي البَابَ.⁩ ⁧رَجَاءً⁩ Please. ⁧رَجَاءً، لَا تَتَكَلَّمُوا بِصَوْتٍ عَالٍ.⁩ ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ Is it possible...? ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُغْلِقَ النَّافِذَةَ؟⁩ Formula Example ⁧تَفَضَّلْ⁩ + imperative .... ⁧تَفَضَّلْ، اُدْخُلْ.⁩ ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ is mainly used to attract attention or for a small request to a stranger (at the bar, on the street); ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ It's fine everywhere. The signs. In public notices Arabic avoids imperative and uses impersonal forms with an action name (maṣdar): Structure Example Translation ⁧مَمْنُوعٌ⁩ + maṣdar ⁧مَمْنُوعٌ التَّدْخِينُ⁩ Smoking not permitted ⁧الرَّجَاءُ⁩ + maṣdar ⁧الرَّجَاءُ إِغْلَاقُ البَابِ⁩ Please close the door ⁧الرَّجَاءُ عَدَمُ⁩ + maṣdar ⁧الرَّجَاءُ عَدَمُ التَّصْوِيرِ⁩ Please do not photograph ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ + maṣdar (recognize) ⁧يُرْجَى الاِنْتِظَارُ هُنَا⁩ Please wait here Plural imperative ⁧اِرْبِطُوا الأَحْزِمَةَ⁩ Buckle up. / ⁧اِنْتَبِهْ!⁩ ⁧اِنْتَبِهْ! خَطَرٌاِنْتِبَاه!⁩ Attention! Danger On the signs words are usually without vowels and often without article or with only structure: ⁧ممنوع التدخين⁩ , ⁧الدخول⁩ , ⁧المخرج. عَدَم⁩ "non" is the negation of the names of action: ⁧عَدَمُ التَّدْخِينِ⁩ Do not smoke. 6. Pronunciation The support wing falls. uktub alone, but wa-ktub, ṯumma ktub; iǧlis, but fa-ǧlis. Do not pronounce the alif waṣla Inside the sentence. The ⁧أَ⁩ of form IV remains. Arsil, wa-arsil (not wa-rsil); aġliq, wa-aġliq. Very short impressions. Here, kun, nam, ḍaʿ, qif, ḫuḏ, kul: a single syllable with short vowel. Say it with a firm tone, but accompany them with ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ . ⁧تَعَالَ⁩ . taʿāla, with the accent on ā long: ta-ʿā-la. Women taʿālay, plural taʿālaw. 7. Listening Script A · Dialog 1 Listen to the dialog 1 without reading it: what must man do, in order? List the shares. Script B · Do or don't do? ⁧١. اُدْخُلْ.⁩ ⁧٢. لَا تَدْخُلْ.⁩ ⁧٣. اِجْلِسِي هُنَا.⁩ ⁧٤. لَا تَتَكَلَّمُوا.⁩ ⁧٥. خُذْ هٰذَا.⁩ ⁧٦. لَا تَنْسَيْ.⁩ ⁧٧. تَعَالَوْا مَعِي.⁩ ⁧٨. قِفْ!⁩ Script C · At the airport ⁧السَّادَةُ المُسَافِرُونَ، اِنْتِبَاه! الرِّحْلَةُ رَقْمُ ٣٢٤ مِنْ مِيلَانُو إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ سَتَتَأَخَّرُ سَاعَةً. الرَّجَاءُ الاِنْتِظَارُ فِي⁩ ⁧القَاعَةِ رَقْمِ ٢. سَيَبْدَأُ الصُّعُودُ فِي السَّاعَةِ الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ مِنَ البَوَّابَةِ رَقْمِ ١٢. جَهِّزُوا جَوَازَاتِ السَّفَرِ⁩ ⁧وَبِطَاقَاتِ الصُّعُودِ. لَا تَتْرُكُوا حَقَائِبَكُمْ دُونَ مُرَاقَبَةٍ. شُكْرًا.⁩ ⁧السَّادَة⁩ • Mr. and Mrs. ⁧الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ⁩ 11 (A2-12) · ⁧جَهِّزُوا⁩ Prepared or preserved meat or meat offal of swine ⁧دُونَ مُرَاقَبَةٍ⁩ • Unattended. 13. Oral production 1. To the door. Playing with the tutor: you are the agent at the door and the tutor an Arabic tourist who has I lost my wallet. Give kind instructions (sit down, fill out, write, sign, wait) and at least two prohibitions. 2. Ask for instructions. Now you are the tourist: ask the tutor how to get to the station and what to do for buy a ticket. Repeat the instructions received to verify that you understand. 3. The right sign. The tutor describes a situation in English (a waiting room of a hospital) you propose two signs in Arabic and read them out loud. 14. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧كْتُبْ⁩ (without alif) ⁧اُكْتُبْ⁩ : two initial consonants → support alf ⁧اُكْتُبْاِكْتُبْ⁩ : the root vowel is u, so ⁧اُ⁩ ⁧اُكْتُبْاِكْتُبْ⁩ ⁧لَا تَذْهَبْلَا اِذْهَبْ⁩ : the ban uses the juxtaposition with the prefix ⁧لَا تَذْهَبْلَا اِذْهَبْ⁩ ⁧اِرْسِلْ⁩ , wa-sil ⁧أَرْسِلْ⁩ , wa-arsil: form IV with ⁧أَ⁩ that does not fall ⁧قُلْنَامْ⁩ , ⁧قُولْ⁩ , ⁧نَمْ⁩ : in the singular imperative the vowel shortens ⁧لَا تَنْسَى⁩ (prohibit) ⁧لَا تَنْسَ⁩ , ⁧اِأْخُذْ⁩ ⁧خُذْاِأْكُلْ⁩ ⁧كُلْ⁩ , imperative naked to a stranger add ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ / ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ 15. title: ‎كَانَand the verbs of his family
text: Lesson overview With ⁧كَانَ⁩ you said "it was" and "it was" (A1-18). In this unit ⁧كَانَ⁩ It becomes an instrument of the story: with the imperfect form the usual past (I lived, I worked, every summer we went...) that in Arabic does not have a proper time. Learn also verbs that work as ⁧كَانَ⁩ and they are used to talk about changes: ⁧صَارَ⁩ and ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ "become', ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ continue to do so. And learn to describe a person: colors, hair, glasses, beard. A week. Item Details Code A2-07 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites Module test A2.1 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 61 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-07), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use ⁧كَانَ⁩ in all the times and ways studied, with the predicate to the accusative; 2. narrating past habits and situations with ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect, distinguishing them from punctual actions to perfect; 3. talk about changes with ⁧صَارَ⁩ and ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ , and what goes on with ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ ; 4. describe the appearance of a person: height, body shape, hair, colors, special signs; 5. read a vocalized text without endings, as you read aloud a modern text. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · sections 1–2: ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect · exercises 1–3 2 Sections 3–4: become, continue · exercises 4–5 · vocabulary 3 Section 5: describe a person · exercise 6 · C script 4 Section 6: read without loss · read 1 · year 10 5 Exercises 7–9 · reading 2 · writing 6 Session with the tutor: telling past habits 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · How was Milan? After the lesson, Luke and Salmā They drink tea at the bar under the school. Arabic Transliteration Translation Lūkā: munḏu matā taskunīna fī Mīlānū Luca: Since you lived in Milan, ⁧مُنْذُ مَتَى تَسْكُنِينَ فِي مِيلَانُو يَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ yā Salmā? Salmā? ⁧سَلْمَى؟⁩ Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مُنْذُ سَنَوَاتٍ كَثِيرَةٍ! عِنْدَمَا جِئْتُ،⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧كُنْتُ طَالِبَةً فِي الجَامِعَةِ.⁩ Salmā: munḏu sanawātin kaṯīra! ʿindamā ǧiʾtu, kuntu ṭālibatan fī l- ǧāmiʿa. Salmā: For many years! When I got here, I was a college student. ⁧وَكَيْفَ كَانَتِ المَدِينَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-kayfa kānati l-madīna? And what was the city like? ⁧كَانَتْ مُخْتَلِفَةً. كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ فِي غُرْفَةٍ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧صَغِيرَةٍ، وَكَانَ الإِيجَارُ رَخِيصًا. لَمْ تَكُنْ هُنَاكَ⁩ ⁧مَطَاعِمُ عَرَبِيَّةٌ كَثِيرَةٌ.⁩ Salmā: kānat muḫtalifa. kuntu askunu fī ġurfatin ṣaġīra, wa-kāna l-īǧāru raḫīṣan. lam takun hunāka maṭāʿimu ʿarabiyyatun kaṯīra. Salmā: It was different. I lived in a small room, and the rent was cheap. There weren't many Arab restaurants. ⁧وَمَاذَا كُنْتِ تَفْعَلِينَ فِي المَسَاءِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-māḏā kunti tafʿalīna fī l- masāʾ? Reading a text without termination Up to now the course texts have been vocized in full, including the final vowels of the cases. In reality, almost no one reads a modern text with all the endings: they read the words with their internal vowels and let the final vowel fall, as in the reading on pause. Reading 1 of this unit is written as follows: internal vowels yes, endings no. What falls: the final vowels of the cases and the tanwīn names and adjectives ( ⁧المَدِينَة⁩ , ⁧شَقَّة صَغِيرَة⁩ ), and the final -u of the imperfect ( ⁧يَعْمَل⁩ , ⁧نَلْعَب⁩ ). What remains written: • the tanwīn -an ( ⁧بَارِدا⁩ , ⁧مُزْدَحِما⁩ ), which reads -a pause or -an if you want; • the personal suffixes of the verbs and the -a of the perfect ( ⁧كَانُوا⁩ , ⁧يَسْكُنُونَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَتْ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ ): are not case-law; • vowels that are part of the word ( ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ , ⁧الآنَ⁩ , ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ ) and vowels ( ⁧مِنَ المَحَطَّة⁩ , ⁧كَانَتِ المَدِينَة⁩ ); • the vowels of suffix pronouns ( ⁧نَفْسِهَا⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَنَا⁩ ); • tāʾ marbūṭa , which reads -a, or -at when the word is the first term of a 'iḍāfa ( ⁧كُرَة القَدَم⁩ → kurat al- qadam). title: The pluralities between: the most frequent patterns
text: Lesson overview More than half of the Arab names form the plural not with a suffix ( ⁧ـُونَ⁩ , ⁧ـَات⁩ ) but changing the scheme of the word: ⁧كِتَاب⁩ → ⁧كُتُب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ → ⁧مَكَاتِب⁩ , ⁧وَزِير⁩ → ⁧وُزَرَاء⁩ . It is the plural over ( ⁧جَمْعُ التَّكْسِير⁩ , is broken plural). In A1 you have learned the plurals one by one; Here you learn to recognize the twelve most frequent patterns, which cover the vast majority of the plurals that you will encounter in the texts. Two practical rules guide everything: the plural is learned with the singular, and the scheme helps you to find the singular when you look for a word in the dictionary. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-08 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites A2-07 exceeded; name schemes (A2-01) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 62–63 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-08), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the twelve most frequent plural patterns and bring a plural back to its singular; 2. actively use the plurals of the high-frequency words of the vocabulary A1–A2; 3. decline the diptotic plurals (fuʿalāʾ, afʿilāʾ, mafāʿil, mafāʿīl, fawāʿil, faʿāʾil); 4. to give adjectives and verbs with the plurals of people and things; 5. use collective names with their unit name ( ⁧تُفَّاح⁩ / ⁧تُفَّاحَة⁩ ); 6. Shopping in the market and describing a place full of people and things. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: healthy and plural plural over · exercise 1 2 Section 2: schemes 1–5 (afʿāl, fuʿūl, fiʿāl, fuʿul, fuʿʿāl) · year 2 3 Section 6: collectives · market vocabulary · script C 4 Reading 1 · year 11 5 Section 4: agreement · year 5 6 Pronunciation · Anki: plural words of A1 7 Review · Writing: list and description to the plural 8 Section 3: schemes 6–12 · year 3 9 Section 5: the diptotes · exercise 4 10 Dialogue 2 · lexicon (second half) · exercise 6 11 Section 7: from plural to dictionary · exercises 7–8 12 Reading 2 (without termination) · script B · exercises 9–10 and 12 13 Session with the tutor: describe an office · writing 14 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · To the market Saturday morning, Luke accompanies Karīm to the market in Via Padova. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧هٰذَا أَحْسَنُ سُوقٍ فِي مِيلَانُو! هُنَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧فَوَاكِهُ وَخُضَارٌ مِنْ كُلِّ البِلَادِ.⁩ Karīm: hāḏā aḥsanu sūqin fī Mīlānū! hunā fawākihu wa-ḫuḍārun min kulli l- bilād. Karīm: This is the best market in Milan! Here there are fruits and vegetables from all countries. ⁧وَالأَسْعَارُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-l-asʿār? What about the prices? ⁧كِيلُو البُرْتُقَالِ بِيُورُو⁩ : ⁧رَخِيصَةٌ. اُنْظُرْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧وَاحِدٍ.⁩ Karīm: raḫīṣa. unẓur: kīlū l-burtuqāli bi-yūrū wāḥid. Karīm: Economics. Look, a kilo of oranges for one euro. ⁧تَفَضَّلُوا يَا شَبَابُ! عِنْدِي طَمَاطِمُ⁩ : ⁧البَائِعُ⁩ ⁧وَبَيْضٌ وَتُفَّاحٌ أَحْمَرُ.⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: tafaḍḍalū yā šabāb! ʿindī ṭamāṭimu wa-bayḍun wa-tuffāḥun aḥmar. Please, guys! I have tomatoes, eggs and red apples. ⁧أُرِيدُ كِيلُو طَمَاطِمَ وَعَشْرَ بَيْضَاتٍ، مِنْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧فَضْلِكَ.⁩ Karīm: urīdu kīlū ṭamāṭima wa-ʿašra bayḍāt, min faḍlik. Karīm: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes and ten eggs, please. ⁧وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ ثَلَاثَ تُفَّاحَاتٍ فَقَطْ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-anā urīdu ṯalāṯa tuffāḥātin faqaṭ. Luca: And I only want three apples. ⁧ثَلَاثُ تُفَّاحَاتٍ؟ خُذْهَا، هَدِيَّةٌ⁩ : ⁧البَائِعُ⁩ ⁧لِلضُّيُوفِ!⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: ṯalāṯu tuffāḥāt? ḫuḏhā, hadiyyatun li-ḍ-ḍuyūf! The seller: Three apples? Take them, they're a guest gift! ⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! النَّاسُ هُنَا كُرَمَاءُ جِدًّا.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: šukran ǧazīlan! an-nāsu hunā kuramāʾu ǧiddan. Thank you so much! The people here are very generous. Karīm: wa-t-tuǧǧāru aḏkiyāʾ: al-āna Karīm: And traders are smart: ⁧وَالتُّجَّارُ أَذْكِيَاءُ: الآنَ سَتَشْتَرِي كُلَّ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ sa-taštarī kulla šayʾin Minh! Now you'll buy everything from him! ⁧شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ!⁩ What to notice. ⁧فَوَاكِه⁩ , ⁧أَسْعَار⁩ , ⁧طَمَاطِم⁩ , ⁧ضُيُوف⁩ , ⁧كُرَمَاء⁩ , ⁧تُجَّار⁩ , ⁧أَذْكِيَاء⁩ They're plural over, each with his own pattern. ⁧خُضَار⁩ ... ⁧تُفَّاح⁩ "Apple' means apples, ⁧بَيْض⁩ "eggs" are collective: they indicate the thing in general; to count you use the unit name in -a ( ⁧تُفَّاحَة⁩ • an apple • • • • • • • • • • • • ⁧بَيْضَة⁩ (a) with the plural in -āt ( ⁧ثَلَاثُ تُفَّاحَاتٍ⁩ , ⁧عَشْرُ بَيْضَاتٍ⁩ ). ⁧كُرَمَاءُ⁩ and ⁧أَذْكِيَاءُ⁩ do not have tanwīn: are diptotes (section 5). ⁧أَحْسَنُ سُوقٍ⁩ The best market is: A2-11. ⁧هَدِيَّة⁩ "Gift" is in the vocabulary. 2. Plural healthy or plural over? Type How it forms Who uses it? Examples healthy male singular + ⁧ـُونَ⁩ / ⁧ـِينَ⁩ many participants and nisba indicating persons (A1-15) , ⁧مُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ , ⁧مُوَظَّفُونَ⁩ ⁧مِصْرِيُّونَ⁩ healthy female singular (without ⁧ة⁩ ) + ⁧ـَات⁩ almost all women's names in ⁧ة⁩ , many names of what in ⁧ة⁩ Long action names, many foreign words , ⁧سَيَّارَات⁩ , ⁧مُوَظَّفَات⁩ ⁧بَاصَات⁩ , ⁧اِجْتِمَاعَات⁩ over changes the scheme most basic names and many adjectives, ⁧وُزَرَاء⁩ , ⁧رِجَال⁩ , ⁧كُتُب⁩ internal ⁧مَكَاتِب⁩ There is no sure rule that says which plural takes a name: the dictionary always indicates the plural next to the singular (A2-01Section 7). But there are useful trends: the names of three consonants with short vowels ( ⁧كَلْب⁩ , ⁧وَلَد⁩ , ⁧قَلَم⁩ ) almost always have a plural over; long words with prefix ⁧مُـ⁩ which indicate people almost always take healthy plural ( ⁧مُدَرِّسُونَ⁩ ); prefix names ⁧مَـ⁩ of place take mafāʿil ( ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ → ⁧مَكَاتِب⁩ ). 3. The most frequent plural patterns The first five families are 'triptote' and decline normally; the other seven are diptote (section 5). title: L'iḍāfa with adjectives and chains of iḍāfa
text: Lesson overview L'iḍāfa (A1-10) is the most frequent construction of the institutional language: ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ , ⁧وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ . In titles and documents it extends in chains of three or four names ( ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ لَجْنَةِ الشُّؤُونِ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ ) and combines with adjectives that all go to the bottom. In this unit you learn to build and above all to unmount these chains, to use the duals and the healthy plurals inside theiḍāfa and the quantifiers are each, all, some, the same, most of them. The vocabulary is that of the organigrams: who directs what. A week. Item Details Code A2-09 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites A2-08 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 64 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-09), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. build and analyse chains of iḍāfa of three and four names; 2. place the adjective at the bottom of the chain and understand what name it refers to; 3. use the male dual and plural healthy as the first term ( ⁧مُوَظَّفُو الوِزَارَةِ⁩ , ⁧وَزِيرَا الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ ); 4. use ⁧كُلّ⁩ , ⁧بَعْض⁩ , ⁧جَمِيع⁩ , ⁧مُعْظَم⁩ , ⁧نَفْس⁩ , ⁧غَيْر⁩ , ⁧عِدَّة⁩ with the right case and determination; 5. read an organization chart and unvoiceless institutional titles and present an institution in 80 words. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: the chains · exercises 1–2 2 Section 2: the adjective at the bottom · exercise 3 · vocabulary 3 Section 3: dual and healthy plural · section 4: quantifiers · exercises 4–5 4 Reading 1 (Organisational) and reading 2 (Titles) · financial years 9–10 5 Listening · Exercises 6–8 · writing 6 Session with the tutor: explain an organization chart 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. What about that lady? ⁧رَئِيسَةُ قِسْمِ الجَوَازَاتِ الجَدِيدَةُ.⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧جَاءَتْ مِنْ فَرْعِ رُومَا.⁩ Hudā: raʾīsatu qismi l-ǧawāzāti l- ǧadīda. ǧāʾat min farʿi Rūmā. Hudā: The new head of the passport section. It's from Rome. ⁧وَمَنْ يَعْمَلُ مَعَ المُتَرْجِمِينَ؟⁩ : ⁧بَاوْلُو⁩ Bāwlū: wa-man yaʿmalu maʿa l- mutarǧimīn? Paul: And who works with translators? ⁧كُلُّ المُوَظَّفِينَ تَقْرِيبًا! مُتَرْجِمُو⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧المَكْتَبِ يُسَاعِدُونَ جَمِيعَ الأَقْسَامِ.⁩ Hudā: kullu l-muwaẓẓafīna taqrīban! mutarǧimū l-maktabi yusāʿidūna ǧamīʿa l-aqsām. Hudā: Almost all employees! Office translators help all sections. ⁧وَهَلْ مُعْظَمُهُمْ عَرَبٌ؟⁩ : ⁧بَاوْلُو⁩ Bāwlū: wa-hal muʿẓamuhum ʿarab? Paul: And most of them are Arabs? ⁧بَعْضُهُمْ عَرَبٌ وَبَعْضُهُمْ إِيطَالِيُّونَ.⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧كَرِيم وَسَارَة مُتَرْجِمَا اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ.⁩ Hudā: baʿḍuhum ʿarabun wa-baʿḍuhum īṭāliyyūn. Karīm wa-Sāra mutarǧimā l- luġati l-ʿarabiyya. Hudā: Some are Arabs and some are Italians. Karīm and Sāra are the two Arabic translators. ⁧وَأَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ رَئِيسِ قِسْمِ شُؤُونِ⁩ : ⁧بَاوْلُو⁩ ⁧الأَجَانِبِ؟⁩ Bāwlū: wa-ayna maktabu raʾīsi qismi šuʾūni l-aǧānib? Paul: And where is the office of the head of foreign affairs? ⁧فِي الطَّابِقِ نَفْسِهِ، فِي آخِرِ المَمَرِّ.⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧تَعَالَ مَعِي!⁩ Hudā: fī ṭ-ṭābiqi nafsih, fī āḫiri l- mamarr. taʿāla maʿī! Chains of iḍāfa A chain is a series of iḍāfa One inside the other. The Rules of A1-10 apply to each ring: 1. only the last name can have the article (or be a proper name, or have a suffix pronoun); 2. all names except the first one are at the genitive; 3. the first name has the case that gives it its function in the sentence; 4. no name of the chain, except the last one, has the article or the tanwīn; 5. the last name decides whether the whole chain is determined or not. Chain Analysis Translation ⁧مَكْتَبُ المُدِيرِ⁩ office + of the Director the Director's office ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الشَّرِكَةِ⁩ office + director + company the office of the director of the company ⁧بَابُ مَكْتَبِ مُدِيرِ الشَّرِكَةِ⁩ door + office + director + company the door of the company's director's office ⁧رَئِيسُ وُزَرَاءِ لُبْنَانَ⁩ President + Ministers + Lebanon the Prime Minister of Lebanon Chain Analysis Translation ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ شَرِكَةٍ⁩ ... + of a company (undetermined) the office of the director of a company How to dismount a chain without vowels. Read from right: the first name without article opens the chain; any name without the following article is a new ring; the first name with the article (or a proper name, or a suffix pronoun) closes it. ⁧مكتب مدير الشركة: مكتب⁩ (opens) ⁧مدير⁩ (Ring) ⁧الشركة⁩ (closes). Adjectives and chains An adjective cannot enter the chain: it is put at the bottom, after the last name, and agrees (genre, number, case, determination) with the name to which it refers. title: Suffixed pronouns on verbs and prepositions
text: Lesson overview "I call you tomorrow," "I have seen it" , "dammelo" , "ammelo" said to me: "in Arabic the pronoun complement is not a separate word, but a suffix attached to the verb" ( ⁧رَأَيْتُهُ⁩ I have seen it, or at the preposition ( ⁧قَالَ لِي⁩ He told me. The suffixes you know from the names (A1-09); Here you use them systematically on verbs, with the small shape changes they require, and complete the preposition table. The context is that of phone calls and messages between colleagues: asking for a favor, offering help, leaving a message. A week. Item Details Code A2-10 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites A2-09 exceeded; suffix pronouns on names (A1-09, A1-12) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 65 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-10), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. attach pronouns to verbs to the perfect, imperfect and imperative, with "mi" = ⁧ـنِي⁩ ; 2. apply shape changes: -tum + suffix → -tumū-, loss of breath, support; 3. use all prepositions with suffixes, including ⁧إِلَيَّ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيَّ⁩ , ⁧فِيَّ⁩ , ⁧لَدَيَّ⁩ ; 4. recognise ⁧إِيَّا⁩ with the second complement ( ⁧أَعْطَانِي إِيَّاهُ⁩ ); 5. phone calls, answer the phone, leave and understand a message; ask and offer a favor. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: suffixes on verbs · exercises 1–2 2 Section 3: changes in form · exercise 3 · vocabulary 3 Sections 4–5: prepositions and two complements · exercises 4–6 4 Section 6: on the phone · exercises 7–9 · reading · exercise 10 5 Listening · Exercise 12 · writing (exercise 11) 6 Session with the tutor: ask and offer help 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · Will you do me a favor? Tuesday night. Karīm Call Luca. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَلُو؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: alū? Hello? ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ يَا لُوكَا، مَعَكَ كَرِيم. هَلْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧أُزْعِجُكَ؟⁩ Karīm: masāʾu l-ḫayri yā Lūkā, maʿaka Karīm. hal uzʿiǧuk? Karīm: Good evening, Luke, I am Karīm. Am I disturbing you? Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧لَا أَبَدًا! تَفَضَّلْ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: lā abadan! tafaḍḍal. Luca: No! Tell me. ⁧أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مُسَاعَدَتِكَ. أُمِّي فِي⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧المُسْتَشْفَى، وَيَجِبُ أَنْ أَزُورَهَا غَدًا صَبَاحًا.⁩ Karīm: aḥtāǧu ilā musāʿadatik. ummī fī l-mustašfā, wa-yaǧibu an azūrahā ġadan ṣabāḥan. Karīm: I need your help. My mom's in the hospital and I have to go see her in the morning. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْهَا! كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: lā baʾsa ʿalayhā! kayfa usāʿiduk? Luca: Let him get better soon! How can I help you? ⁧تَرْجَمْتُ تَقْرِيرَ الأُسْبُوعِ، لٰكِنِّي لَمْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧أُرْسِلْهُ إِلَى المُفَوَّضِ. هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُ⁩ ⁧إِيَّاهُ؟⁩ Karīm: tarǧamtu taqrīra l-usbūʿ, lākinnī lam ursilhu ilā l-mufawwaḍ. hal yumkinu an tuʿṭiyahu iyyāh? Karīm: I translated the report of the week, but I did not send it to the Commissioner. Can you give it to him? ⁧طَبْعًا. أَيْنَ وَضَعْتَهُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ṭabʿan. ayna waḍaʿtah? Sure. Where did you put it? ⁧فِي دُرْجِ مَكْتَبِي. المِفْتَاحُ عِنْدَ هُدَى،⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧اُطْلُبْهُ مِنْهَا.⁩ Karīm: fī durǧi maktabī. al-miftāḥu ʿinda Hudā, uṭlubhu minhā. Karīm: In my desk drawer. The key has it. HudāAsk her. ⁧حَاضِر. وَإِذَا سَأَلَنِي المُفَوَّضُ عَنْكَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ḥāḍir. wa-iḏā saʾalanī l- mufawwaḍu ʿank? Okay. What if the commissioner asks me about you? ⁧قُلْ لَهُ إِنِّي سَأَتَّصِلُ بِهِ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ.⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، أَنْتَ أَخٌ!⁩ Karīm: qul lahu innī sa-attaṣilu bihi baʿda ẓ-ẓuhr. šukran ǧazīlan, anta aḫ! Karīm: Tell him I'll call him in the afternoon. Thank you so much, you're a brother! Lūkā: lā šukra ʿalā wāǧib. sallim lī ʿalā You're welcome. Say hello to me. ⁧لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ. سَلِّمْ لِي عَلَى⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ummik. Mother. ⁧أُمِّكَ.⁩ What to notice. ⁧أُزْعِجُكَ⁩ - you are disturbing, ⁧أَزُورَهَا⁩ • the visit • • ⁧أُسَاعِدُكَ⁩ I'll help you. ⁧أُرْسِلْهُ⁩ (i) I sent it, ⁧وَضَعْتَهُ⁩ You put it in, ⁧اُطْلُبْهُ⁩ • ask for it (the key) • ⁧سَأَلَنِي⁩ "The pronoun complement is a suffix of the verb; for ... the suffix is ⁧ـنِي. تُعْطِيَهُ إِيَّاهُ⁩ • give it (give it to it) • when the complements are two pronouns, the second one leans on ⁧إِيَّا⁩ (Section 5). ⁧لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْهِ⁩ / ⁧عَلَيْهَا⁩ is the wish to those who have a sick person: "Nothing serious for him/her" . ⁧لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ⁩ "We do not thank ourselves for a duty" is a thank you. ⁧سَلِّمْ لِي عَلَى⁩ - Say hello to me... ⁧حَاضِر⁩ It is well used in Egypt and the Levant. ⁧إِذَا⁩ If the following conditions are met:A2-14); ⁧إِنِّي⁩ I'll do it later. ⁧قُلْ⁩ ( A2-19). 2. The supplementary pronouns on verbs The suffixes are those of the names (A1-09), with only one difference: ⁧ـنِي⁩ ( -nī), no ⁧ـِي⁩ . The suffix does not change the verb , which maintains its desinence: ⁧سَاعَدَهُ⁩ ( sāʿada-hu), ⁧يُسَاعِدُهُ⁩ ( yusāʿidu-hu), ⁧أَنْ يُسَاعِدَهُ⁩ (subjunctive), ⁧لَمْ يُسَاعِدْهُ⁩ (Giussive). In pause reading the suffix remains whole: yusāʿiduhu, yusāʿid. ⁧ـهُ⁩ becomes ⁧ـهِ⁩ after i, ī, ay, as on names (A1-09) and with prepositions ( ⁧بِهِ⁩ , ⁧فِيهِ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ Section 4): ⁧يُعْطِيهِ⁩ yuʿṭīhi "Gives it', ⁧رَأَيْتِهِ⁩ raʾaytihi You have seen it (you, f.) ⁧اُكْتُبِيهِ⁩ uktubīhi Write it to a woman. Without vowels the difference is not seen: ⁧يعطيه⁩ , ⁧رأيته⁩ . 3. Changes in form Case Rule Example verb -ū (they) the alif mute falls ⁧كَتَبُوا⁩ + ⁧هُ⁩ → ⁧كَتَبُوهُ⁩ They wrote it down. verb in -tum (voi) -tum becomes -tumū- ⁧رَأَيْتُمْ⁩ + ⁧هُ⁩ → ⁧رَأَيْتُمُوهُ⁩ You've seen it. Jurissive and imperative in sukūn the suffix attacks directly ⁧لَمْ أَرَهُ⁩ I didn't see it. ⁧اُكْتُبْهُ⁩ • Write it down · ⁧خُذْهَا⁩ Take it. weak imperative the short form remains ⁧أَعْطِنِي⁩ "Dammi" ⁧قُلْ لَهُ⁩ Of a kind used in the manufacture of goods of heading 84.03 defects in -ā the ā is written with ⁧ا⁩ in front of the suffix ⁧أَعْطَى⁩ + ⁧نِي⁩ → ⁧أَعْطَانِي⁩ "He gave me " ⁧رَأَى⁩ + ⁧هُ⁩ → ⁧رَآهُ⁩ He saw it. imperfect with -na (5 persons) -na remains at the signpost, falls to the conjunctive and the juxive ⁧يَعْرِفُونَهُ⁩ They know him. ⁧لَمْ يَعْرِفُوهُ⁩ They didn't know him. ⁧رَآهُ.⁩ ⁧رَأَى⁩ + ⁧هُ⁩ It is written with the Madda: ⁧رَآهُ⁩ raʾāhu He saw it. ⁧رَأَتْهُ⁩ You have seen it/you have seen it. The verb "I" to the perfect ends in -you: ⁧رَأَيْتُهُ⁩ I've seen it. ⁧سَاعَدْتُكَ⁩ I helped you. Do not confuse with ?tu (m.) ⁧رَأَيْتَهُ⁩ You have seen it, without vowels you write equal ( ⁧رأيته⁩ ). 4. Verbs with preposition. Many verbs hold a preposition, and the pronoun attaches itself to that: ⁧أَتَّصِلُ بِكَ⁩ I'm calling you. ⁧أَبْحَثُ عَنْهُ⁩ I'm looking for him. ⁧سَأَلَ عَنْكِ⁩ He asked for you, ⁧قُلْتُ لَهَا⁩ I told her, ⁧أَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْكُمْ⁩ I need you. ⁧سَمَحَ لِي⁩ "It allowed me to do so," ⁧رَدَّ عَلَيْنَا⁩ He replied to us. Always learn the verb with his preposition: in English he often does not exist. 5. Two complements: ⁧إِيَّا⁩ Some verbs have two direct complements: ⁧أَعْطَى⁩ • give and ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ • ask for • ⁧سَأَلْتُهُ سُؤَالًا⁩ I asked him a question. Complements Example Translation two names ⁧أَعْطَيْتُ لُوكَا المِفْتَاحَ.⁩ I gave Luca the key. pronoun + name ⁧أَعْطَيْتُهُ المِفْتَاحَ.⁩ I gave him the key. two pronouns ⁧أَعْطَيْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ.⁩ I gave it to him. When the second complement is also a pronoun, it does not stick to the verb but to ⁧إِيَّا⁩ + suffix: ⁧إِيَّاهُ⁩ , ⁧إِيَّاهَا⁩ , ⁧إِيَّاهُمْ⁩ . It is a construction to be recognized: in the current use you often prefer to repeat the name ( ⁧أَعْطَيْتُهُ⁩ ⁧المِفْتَاحَ⁩ ). ⁧إِيَّا⁩ it also appears in fixed expressions: ⁧إِيَّاكَ أَنْ⁩ ... woe to thee if... ⁧إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ⁩ We adore you in the first sura of the Qur'an). 6. On the phone and in the messages Situation Formules answer ⁧تَفَضَّلْ.⁩ · ⁧نَعَمْ؟⁩ · ⁧أَلُو؟⁩ Get in. ⁧مَعَكَ لُوكَا.⁩ "I'm Luca" (Lett. A telephone call or a work message between Arabic colleagues almost always begins with a greeting and a question about health before the actual request; To enter into the substance immediately may seem abrupt. Oral production 1. One phone call. Roleplay with the tutor: call an office and ask for a person who is not there; leave a message with name, number and reason. 2. Ask and offer help (session). The tutor presents you with three situations (a link with the broken car, a neighbour Older with the expense, a tourist who has lost his phone): offer help and ask what it takes; Then the tutor asks you a favor and you answer. 3. Who did what? Tell a day of work using at least eight suffix pronouns (I called him, He answered me, I gave him...). 15. title: Comparative and superlative
text: Lesson overview The largest city is: to compare Arabic, it uses only one scheme. afʿal ( ⁧أَفْعَل⁩ ), which gives together comparative and superlative. From ⁧كَبِير⁩ Large ⁧أَكْبَر⁩ • Larger / Largest; from ⁧رَخِيص⁩ Economic ⁧أَرْخَص⁩ . When the adjective doesn't enter the scheme, you use it. ⁧أَكْثَر⁩ Other ⁧أَقَلّ⁩ The least is followed by a name to the accusative. The female form of the superlative, fuʿlā ( ⁧كُبْرَى⁩ , ⁧عُلْيَا⁩ , ⁧أُولَى⁩ ), meets above all in fixed names of politics and geography: here you learn to recognize it. The context is the comparison between cities, prices and hotels, in view of Luca's trip to Cairo. A week. Item Details Code A2-11 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites A2-10 exceeded; root and scheme (A2-01); colors (A2-07); iḍāfa (A2-09) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 66 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-11), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form comparative afʿal by the adjectives of three radicals, including double roots ( ⁧أَقَلّ⁩ ), defective ( ⁧أَغْلَى⁩ ) e with hamza ( ⁧أَهْدَأ⁩ ); 2. compare with ⁧مِنْ⁩ , also with pronouns ( ⁧أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي⁩ ), and grade with ⁧بِكَثِيرٍ⁩ and ⁧قَلِيلًا⁩ ; 3. use ⁧أَكْثَرُ⁩ / ⁧أَقَلُّ⁩ + accusative when the adjective does not have the form afʿal ( ⁧أَكْثَرُ ازْدِحَامًا⁩ ); 4. expressing the superlative in three ways ( ⁧أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَةٍ⁩ , ⁧أَكْبَرُ المُدُنِ⁩ , ⁧المَدِينَةُ الكُبْرَى⁩ ); 5. recognizing female fuʿlā in fixed names ( ⁧القَاهِرَةُ الكُبْرَى⁩ , ⁧المَحْكَمَةُ العُلْيَا⁩ , ⁧الشَّرْقُ الأَوْسَطُ⁩ ); 6. compare two cities and choose from several offers (hotels, products). Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the scheme afʿal · financial years 1–2 2 Section 3: ⁧أَكْثَر⁩ / ⁧أَقَلّ⁩ + charge · exercise 3 · vocabulary 3 Sections 4–5: superlative and fuʿlā · financial years 4–5 4 Section 6: equality and difference · exercises 6–9 · reading · exercise 10 5 Listening · Exercise 12 · writing (exercise 11) 6 Session with the tutor: compare and choose 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · What suitcase? Saturday afternoon. Luca and Maria in a luggage store. Arabic Transliteration Translation al-bāʾiʿa: masāʾa l-ḫayr- Good evening, I can. ⁧مَسَاءَ الخَيْرِ، هَلْ أُسَاعِدُكُمَا؟⁩ : ⁧البَائِعَة⁩ usāʿidukumā? Help you? Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَسَاءَ النُّورِ. أَبْحَثُ عَنْ حَقِيبَةِ سَفَرٍ:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧سَأُسَافِرُ إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ أُسْبُوعَيْنِ.⁩ Lūkā: masāʾa n-nūr. abḥaṯu ʿan ḥaqībati safar: sa-usāfiru ilā l-qāhirati usbūʿayn.
