title: Name Numbers
text: Lesson overview In A1 you have learned the numbers In front of a name, however, the Arabic number follows its own rules, among the most famous of grammar: from three to ten takes the form \"opposed" to the genus of name ( ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ but ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ ), and the counted name changes number and case depending on the digit (plural genitive after 3–10, singular accusative after 11–99, singular genitive after 100 and 1000). In this unit learn the complete system up to millions, years, percentages, fractions, prices in Arab currencies and order them over ten. The rules are many: the objective of A2 is use them well with the most frequent names (days, years, hours, people, euros) and recognize the rest. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-12 Level A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase Prerequisites A2-11 exceeded; Numbers 0 a 10 and dozens (A1-11); order them from 1 a 10 and months (A1-17); plurality (A2-08) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 67–68 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-12), scripts for speech synthesis, receipts and flyers with prices, session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use .......................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... ⁧وَاحِد⁩ / ⁧اِثْنَان⁩ as reinforcing) and ⁧أَحَدُ⁩ / ⁧إِحْدَى⁩ • One the one of the following: 2. Numbers to be allocated 3 a 10 with the name (polarity + plural genitive); 3. use numbers from 11 a 99 with the singular accusative, and ⁧كَمْ⁩ + singular accusative; 4. say and read hundreds, thousands, millions and years; 5. slight percentages, fractions and prices in the main Arab currencies; 6. recognizing the ordinals beyond the ten ( ⁧الحَادِي عَشَرَ⁩ , ⁧القَرْنُ الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ ); 7. buy and ask for prices, give personal data and dates, understand figures in a news. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: one and two · exercise 1 2 Section 3: from three to ten · exercises 2–3 · lexicon (first half) 3 Section 4: 11 a 19 · year 4 4 Section 5: 20 a 99 and ⁧كَمْ⁩ · financial years 5–6 5 Reading 1: announcements · exercise 13 6 Script B: dictation of numbers (exercise) 15) · oral production: buy and ask for prices 7 Anki · review of sections 2–5 8 Dialogue 2 · section 7: one hundred, one thousand, millions · year 7 9 Section 8: years and dates · exercise 8 · lexicon (second half) 10 Sections 9–10: percentages, fractions, prices, order books · financial year 9–11 Day Activity 11 Reading 2: a news · exercise 14 · year 12 12 Script C: the figures in the news · writing (exercise 16) 13 Session with the tutor: personal data and dates 14 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · One dinner for ten Saturday morning. Salmā takes Luca to an Egyptian grocery store in Via Padova, Milan. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَهْلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة سَلْمَى! كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: ahlan yā ustāḏa Salmā! kayfa ḥāluki? The storekeeper: Welcome, ma'am Salmā! How are you? ⁧بِخَيْرٍ، الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ. هٰذَا زَمِيلِي لُوكَا.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧عِنْدِي عَشَاءٌ لِعَشَرَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ،⁩ ⁧وَأَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَشْيَاءَ كَثِيرَةٍ.⁩ Salmā: bi-ḫayr, al-ḥamdu li-llāh. hāḏā zamīlī Lūkā. ʿindī ʿašāʾun li-ʿašarati ašḫāṣin yawma s-sabt, wa-aḥtāǧu ilā ašyāʾa kaṯīra. Salmā: Well, thank God. This is my colleague Luca. I have a dinner on Saturday for ten people and I need a lot of things. ⁧تَفَضَّلِي، أَنَا فِي خِدْمَتِكِ.⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: tafaḍḍalī, ana fī ḫidmatiki. The storekeeper: Please, I'm at your disposal. ⁧أُرِيدُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَكْيَاسِ أَرُزٍّ، وَثَلَاثَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧زُجَاجَاتِ زَيْتٍ، وَخَمْسَ عُلَبِ شَايٍ.⁩ Salmā: urīdu arbaʿata akyāsi aruzz, wa-ṯalāṯa zuǧāǧāti zayt, wa-ḫamsa ʿulabi šāy. Salmā: I would like four bags of rice, three bottles of oil and five boxes of tea. ⁧وَالخُبْزُ؟ عِنْدَنَا خُبْزٌ مِصْرِيٌّ اليَوْمَ.⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: wa-l-ḫubz? ʿindanā ḫubzun miṣriyyuni l-yawm. The storekeeper: What about the bread? Today we have Egyptian bread. ⁧مُمْتَاز! اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَغِيفًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: mumtāz! iṯnay ʿašara raġīfan, min faḍlik. SalmāGreat! 12 loaves, please. ⁧وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ عُلْبَتَيْ قَهْوَةٍ. بِكَمِ العُلْبَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-ana urīdu ʿulbatay qahwa. bi- kami l-ʿulba? And I'd like two packs of coffee. How much is one? ⁧العُلْبَةُ بِأَرْبَعَةِ يُورُو، وَالعُلْبَتَانِ بِسَبْعَةٍ⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ ⁧فَقَطْ.⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: al-ʿulbatu bi-arbaʿati yūrū, wa- l-ʿulbatāni bi-sabʿatin faqaṭ. The storekeeper: One costs four euros, two only seven. ⁧سِعْرٌ مُمْتَازٌ!⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: siʿrun mumtāz! Good price! … ⁧أَرُزٌّ، زَيْتٌ، شَايٌ، خُبْزٌ، قَهْوَةٌ⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ ⁧المَجْمُوعُ سِتَّةٌ وَأَرْبَعُونَ يُورُو وَنِصْفٌ.⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: aruzz, zayt, šāy, ḫubz, qahwa… al-maǧmūʿu sittatun wa- arbaʿūna yūrū wa-niṣf. The shopkeeper: Rice, oil, tea, bread, coffee... The total is forty-six euro and a half. ⁧تَفَضَّلْ، خَمْسُونَ يُورُو.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: tafaḍḍal, ḫamsūna yūrū. Salmā: Here you go, 50 euros. ⁧وَهٰذَا البَاقِي: ثَلَاثَةُ يُورُو وَنِصْفٌ.⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: wa-hāḏā l-bāqī: ṯalāṯatu yūrū wa-niṣf. The shopkeeper: And here's the rest: three and a half euros. ⁧مُنْذُ مَتَى تَعْمَلُ فِي هٰذَا المَحَلِّ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: munḏu matā taʿmalu fī hāḏā l- maḥall? Luca: How long have you been working in this store? ⁧مُنْذُ اثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً! جِئْتُ إِلَى⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ ⁧مِيلَانُو عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَأَرْبَعَةٍ.⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: munḏu ṯnatayni wa-ʿišrīna sana! ǧiʾtu ilā Mīlānū ʿāma alfayni wa- arbaʿa. The storekeeper: For 22 years! I arrived in Milan in 2004. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧هُوَ يَعْرِفُ كُلَّ المِصْرِيِّينَ فِي الحَيِّ!⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: huwa yaʿrifu kulla l-miṣriyyīna fī l-ḥayy! Salmā: He knows all the Egyptians in the neighborhood! ⁧خَمْسَمِئَةٍ فَقَطْ!⁩ … ⁧لَا، لَيْسَ كُلَّهُمْ⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ al-bāʾiʿ: lā, laysa kullahum… ḫamsamiʾatin faqaṭ! The storekeeper: No, not all... only 500! ⁧أَرُزّ⁩ (') rice () ' ⁧كِيس⁩ (pl. ⁧أَكْيَاس⁩ ) ..... ⁧زَيْت⁩ Oil (s) ⁧عَشَاء⁩ Dinner. What to notice. ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ أَكْيَاسٍ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَ زُجَاجَاتٍ⁩ , ⁧خَمْسَ عُلَبٍ⁩ , ⁧عَشَرَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ⁩ : 3 a 10 the name goes to the plural genitive and the number has the shape with ⁧ة⁩ if the singular name is male ( ⁧كِيس⁩ , ⁧شَخْص⁩ ), without ⁧ة⁩ if you are female ( ⁧زُجَاجَة⁩ , ⁧عُلْبَة⁩ ). Here the number is charged because it complements ⁧أُرِيدُ. اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَغِيفًا⁩ , ⁧اِثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً⁩ : 11 a 99 The name goes to the singular accusative. ⁧عُلْبَتَيْ قَهْوَةٍ⁩ : for two is enough the dual, here in iḍāfa without ⁧ن⁩ ( A2-09). ⁧خَمْسَمِئَةٍ⁩ "Five hundred" . ⁧عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَأَرْبَعَةٍ⁩ In 2004(Section 8). ⁧يُورُو⁩ It's unchangeable. ⁧أُسْتَاذ⁩ / ⁧أُسْتَاذَة⁩ , in addition to the "professor" , in Egypt is a title of respect for an educated person. 2. One and two. Number With a name Reinforced Translation 1 · ⁧كِتَابٌ⁩ ⁧كِتَابٌ وَاحِدٌسَيَّارَةٌ⁩ ⁧سَيَّارَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ⁩ · a book · one machine 2 · ⁧كِتَابَانِ⁩ ⁧كِتَابَانِ اثْنَانِسَيَّارَتَانِ⁩ ⁧سَيَّارَتَانِ اثْنَتَانِ⁩ · two books · two (and no more) machines “One” uses the singular noun; “two” uses the dual. Not said. ⁧وَاحِد كِتَاب⁩ . ⁧وَاحِد⁩ and ⁧اِثْنَان⁩ are added after the name, as adjectives that agree, only to insist on the number: ⁧غُرْفَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَطْ⁩ One room is one. One of them, one of them. ⁧أَحَدُ⁩ ( m.) / ⁧إِحْدَى⁩ (f.) + plural determined, in iḍāfa: ⁧أَحَدُ الطُّلَّابِ⁩ • one of the students • ⁧إِحْدَى المُوَظَّفَاتِ⁩ (a) one of the employees (a) ⁧أَحَدُهُمْ⁩ One of them is. In the news it is very frequent: ⁧أَحَدُ المَسْؤُولِينَ⁩ • a person in charge. 3. Three to ten: polarity Number With a male name With a female name 3  ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ 4  ⁧أَرْبَعُ سَنَوَاتٍأَرْبَعَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ 5  ⁧خَمْسُ نِسَاءٍخَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ 6  ⁧سِتُّ سَاعَاتٍسِتَّةُ أَشْخَاصٍ⁩ 7  ⁧سَبْعُ لَيَالٍسَبْعَةُ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ 8  ⁧ثَمَانِي طَالِبَاتٍثَمَانِيَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ 9  ⁧تِسْعُ دَقَائِقَتِسْعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ⁩ 10  ⁧عَشْرُ غُرَفٍعَشَرَةُ مَكَاتِبَ⁩ Three rules: 1. The number comes first and the name follows it in iḍāfa, to the undetermined plural genitive: ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ . 2. Polarity. If the singular name is masculine, the number has the ⁧ة⁩ ; If it's feminine, it doesn't. Count on singular, not plural: ⁧رَجُل⁩ ( m.) → ⁧خَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ ; ⁧اِمْرَأَة⁩ ( f.) → ⁧خَمْسُ نِسَاءٍ⁩ ; ⁧لَيْلَة⁩ ( f.) → ⁧سَبْعُ لَيَالٍ⁩ , although ⁧لَيَالٍ⁩ has no ⁧ة⁩ . 3. The number declines as a name: ⁧رَأَيْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ رِجَالٍ⁩ I saw three men. ⁧فِي خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ⁩ In five days. The name stays with the genitive. Attention to shapes. ⁧عَشَرَةُ⁩ ( ʿašaratu) with male children, ⁧عَشْرُ⁩ ( ʿašru) with the female: also the vowel changes. ⁧ثَمَانِيَةُ⁩ with males, ⁧ثَمَانِي⁩ ( ṯamānī) with women. The diptotes remain such: ⁧سَبْعَةُ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ , ⁧تِسْعُ دَقَائِقَ⁩ ( A2-08). With the article the number usually follows the name as adjective: ⁧الأَيَّامُ الثَّلَاثَةُ⁩ The three-day period shall be: ⁧السَّنَوَاتُ الخَمْسُ⁩ The five years are the same. It is also found ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ الأَيَّامِ⁩ , less frequent. A trick to remember. With the male names the number appears feminine, and vice versa. Think about ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ and ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَاعَاتٍ⁩ like models and repeat them until they sound natural. 4. From 11 a 19 Number With a male name With a female name 11  ⁧إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًأَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ 12  ⁧اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًاِثْنَا عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ 13  ⁧ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةًثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ 14  ⁧أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةًأَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ 15  ⁧خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ دَقِيقَةًخَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ 16  ⁧سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ سَاعَةًسِتَّةَ عَشَرَ شَخْصًا⁩ 17  ⁧سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ سَاعَةًسَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ شَخْصًا⁩ 18  ⁧ثَمَانِيَ عَشْرَةَ صَفْحَةًثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩ 19 ⁧تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ صَفْحَةًتِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩ The rules: 1. The name goes to the singular indeterminate accusative: ⁧خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ (Lett. 15 as per day). 2. 11 and 12 they agree in both parts: ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ⁩ ( m.) / ⁧إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ⁩ ( f.). 3. From 13 a 19 the unit follows polarity (as 3–9), the second part shall agree: ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً⁩ . 4. The two sides end up in -a and don't decline, except 12: ⁧اِثْنَا عَشَرَ⁩ (name) / ⁧اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ⁩ (genitive and The Court ruled: ⁧عَشَرَ⁩ and ⁧عَشْرَةَ⁩ . In numbers 11–19, with the male they say ʿašara (without ⁧ة⁩ ), with women ʿašrata (with ⁧ة⁩ and without vowel on the š): the opposite of what happens with the 10 alone. 5. From 20 a 99, e ⁧كَمْ⁩ The tens have only one form for the two genera and decline as a healthy plural: -ūna the name, -īna to the genitive and the accusative. Ten Name Genitive / Accusative 20  ⁧عِشْرِينَعِشْرُونَ⁩ 30  ⁧ثَلَاثِينَثَلَاثُونَ⁩ 40  ⁧أَرْبَعِينَأَرْبَعُونَ⁩ 50  ⁧خَمْسِينَخَمْسُونَ⁩ 60  ⁧سِتِّينَسِتُّونَ⁩ 70  ⁧سَبْعِينَسَبْعُونَ⁩ 80  ⁧ثَمَانِينَثَمَانُونَ⁩ 90  ⁧تِسْعِينَتِسْعُونَ⁩ The composite numbers are called units + ⁧وَ⁩ + 10 , as in German (- 1 and 20 ,): Number With a male name With a female name 21  ⁧إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةًوَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ 22  ⁧اِثْنَتَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةًاِثْنَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ 35  ⁧خَمْسٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةًخَمْسَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا⁩ 48  ⁧ثَمَانٍ وَأَرْبَعُونَ سَاعَةًثَمَانِيَةٌ وَأَرْبَعُونَ شَخْصًا⁩ 99 ⁧تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ دَقِيقَةًتِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ يُورُو⁩ The name goes to the singular accusative, as after 11–19. The unit follows the rules of 1–2 (agreement) and 3–9 (polarity); both sides decline: ⁧فِي خَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا⁩ In twenty-five days. title: The structure of the Arabic name
text: Lesson overview A complete Arabic name may contain a lot of information: the proper name, the name of the father and grandfather, a nickname, an origin, sometimes the name of a son. Who reads documents, lists or news must be able to break down a name and understand which part is from "name" and which from "name" because they do not always correspond to the boxes of European forms. This unit opens the trace of onomastics (ONO-01 and ONO-02): here you study the parts of the name and their order; in ONO-02 Latin graphs and variants. A week. Item Details Code ONO-01 Level A2 · Onomastic trace Prerequisites Test A2.2 exceeded; iḍāfa (A2-09); nisba (A1, A2-01) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 70 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (Tag ONO-01), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the five traditional parts of the name: ism, nasab, kunya, laqab, nisba; 2. read and write ⁧ابن⁩ / ⁧بن⁩ / ⁧بنت⁩ and distinguish ⁧آل⁩ The family of the person (s) from Article ⁧الـ⁩ ; 3. recognizing composite names ( ⁧عَبْد الله⁩ , ⁧نُور الدِّين⁩ ) and do not break them; 4. understand how a name appears on documents in different areas of the Arab world; 5. I'll introduce you under the full name and ask someone for his full name. Note of method. A name says something about the traditions of names, not about a person's identity. A Nisba as ⁧المِصْرِيّ⁩ "Egyptian" may be a surname inherited from generations; a name "religious" does not say what the bearer believes; many names pass from one country to another. From a name you never deduce nationality, religion or origin: you read the data of the document and ask the person. Texts. From this unit the texts are partially vocized: vowels on new words, forms in study and where reading is ambiguous; desinences only where they serve. Tables and examples remain vocalized. Plan of the week. It is the name in four parts. ⁧وَمَا اسْمُ عَائِلَتِكِ إِذَنْ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-mā smu ʿāʾilatiki iḏan? Mārkū»! !« ⁧أَبَا مَارْكُو⁩ » What to notice. ⁧كَرِيم بْنُ مُحَمَّد: بْن⁩ “son of” is written without alif between two names (section 3). In the Egyptian name of Salmā There isn't ⁧بْن⁩ : The names are placed one after the other and the link is implied. ⁧الاِسْمُ الرُّبَاعِيُّ⁩ The name is in four parts ( ⁧ثُلَاثِيّ⁩ The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 21 (3) of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. ⁧أُمّ نُور⁩ is the Kunya: it is formed by the name of the eldest son, or a daughter if there are no sons. ⁧يُنَادُونَنِي⁩ They call me "I" ( ⁧يُنَادِي⁩ Call someone, contact them. ⁧بِالضَّبْطِ⁩ Exactly. ⁧لَوْ⁩ … ⁧لَـ⁩ If... then it is the hypothetical period of unreality: for now recognize it. After ⁧كُنْتَ⁩ Kunya goes to the accusative: ⁧أَبَا مَارْكُو⁩ (Section 4). 2. The five parts of the name Part What is it? Example Translation ism ⁧اِسْم⁩ the proper name, given at birth ⁧فَاطِمَة⁩ · ⁧خَالِد⁩ — nasab ⁧نَسَب⁩ the chain •son / daughter of • ⁧خَالِد بْن سَعِيد بْن عُمَر⁩ Ḫālid child of Saʿīd child of ʿUmar kunya ⁧كُنْيَة⁩ If you are a parent of a child, you must have a child. ⁧أُمّ نُور⁩ · ⁧أَبُو يُوسُف⁩ father of Yūsuf · mother of Nūr laqab ⁧لَقَب⁩ nickname, title, epithet ⁧الطَّوِيل⁩ · ⁧الرَّشِيد⁩ the rectum · the sling nisba ⁧نِسْبَة⁩ adjective of origin, group or trade ⁧النَّجَّار⁩ · ⁧الحَلَبِيّ⁩ · ⁧المِصْرِيّ⁩ the Egyptian · of Aleppo · the carpenter In the classic name the parts can appear all, in a fairly fixed order: kunya + ism + nasab + nisba (the laqab can be at the beginning or at the end). Example invented: ⁧أَبُو عَلِيّ الحَسَنُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ البَغْدَادِيُّ⁩ « Abū ʿAlī al- Ḥasan child of Aḥmad, of Baghdad. In the modern name, the parts have changed: the nasab became the chain + father's name + grandpa's name, and many laqab and nisba have become family surnames (section 7). In today's name, then, ⁧حَدَّاد⁩ • blacksmith's or ⁧المِصْرِيّ⁩ The Egyptians are usually only surnames. 3. Nasab: ⁧ابن⁩ , ⁧بن⁩ , ⁧بنت⁩ Form When Example ⁧بْن⁩ (without alif) between two names, when the second is the father of the first ⁧مُحَمَّد بْن سَالِم⁩ ⁧ابْن⁩ (with alif) at the beginning of line or sentence, or when it does not stand between two names ⁧ابْن خَلْدُون⁩ · ⁧هُوَ ابْنُ سَالِم.⁩ ⁧بِنْت⁩ In all positions, the daughter of the child ⁧فَاطِمَة بِنْت عَلِيّ⁩ Pronunciation. Between two names we read bnu / bin: Muḥammadu bnu Sālim, in speech Muḥammad bin Sālim. In the surnames of the Maghreb is often found the form well: ⁧بِن يُوسُف⁩ Ben Youssef. The modern nasab without ⁧بْن⁩ . In much of the Arab world (Egypt, Levant, Iraq) today nasab is written without ⁧بْن⁩ : ⁧أَحْمَد مُحَمَّد عَلِيّ⁩ means "M"Aḥmad, son of Muḥammad, son of ʿAlī». ⁧مُحَمَّد⁩ It is not a middle name as in English "Carlo Alberto": it is the father's name. In the Gulf countries ⁧بْن⁩ / ⁧بِنْت⁩ much is still used in the full names: ⁧سُلْطَان بْن عَلِيّ المَرْزُوقِيّ⁩ . End of nasab in the Maghreb. In Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia ⁧بن⁩ is often part of a fixed surname: ⁧يُوسُف بِن سَالِم⁩ can be simply ...Yūsuf, of the Ben family SālimAnd his father can be called another way. On the documents you can read the box of the father's name, if there is. 4. La kunya: ⁧أبو⁩ and ⁧أم⁩ The Kunya is formed with ⁧أَبُو⁩ (to the accused) ⁧أَبَا⁩ , to the genitive ⁧أَبِي⁩ ) o ⁧أُمّ⁩ + the name of the eldest child: ⁧أَبُو يُوسُف⁩ , ⁧أُمّ كَرِيم⁩ . It is used: • as a respectful and affectionate name, very common in the Levant, Iraq and the Gulf: ⁧يَا أَبَا يُوسُف⁩ ! « Abū Yūsuf!»; • as a traditional nickname, even for those who do not have children: to certain names it is traditionally a kunya; • as a name by which a person is known, instead of his own name: ⁧هُوَ مَعْرُوفٌ بِأَبِي سَامِي⁩ « è known as Abū Sāmī». Attention. ⁧أَبُو⁩ may also be a fixed last name ( ⁧أَبُو زَيْد⁩ , ⁧أَبُو شَقْرَا⁩ are family names) or a place name ( ⁧أَبُو ظَبْي⁩ "Abu Dhabi"). A kunya is not always the father of a real son, and a surname with ⁧أَبُو⁩ She's not a kunya. 5. Laqab and nisba The laqab is an epithet: a title (classical as ⁧الرَّشِيد⁩ The well-guided nickname is a nickname related to appearance or character ( ⁧الطَّوِيل⁩ • the slinger, ⁧الأَسْمَر⁩ "The Brown" is a trade. Many modern surnames come from here. On the documents of certain countries (Algeria, Tunisia, Iraq) the word ⁧اللَّقَب⁩ it is the box "cognome" in question. The nisba is the adjective in -ī which you know (A1): indicates origin ( ⁧المِصْرِيّ⁩ , ⁧الفَاسِيّ⁩ Fès-Fès-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fès-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fés-Fés-Fés-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès-Fès- ⁧الحَلَبِيّ⁩ (Aleppo) belonging to a group or family, or to a trade. Even the nisba have often become surnames: who is called ⁧الحَلَبِيّ⁩ He may have never seen Aleppo today. Crafts become surnames. The scheme faʿʿāl of trades (A2-08) is frequent in surnames: ⁧حَدَّاد⁩ • blacksmith, ⁧نَجَّار⁩ • carpenters, ⁧خَيَّاط⁩ "Sardo" is the name of the manufacturer. ⁧عَطَّار⁩ Scenter, grocery store. As in English Ferrari, Sartori, Fabbri. ⁧آل⁩ and ⁧الـ⁩ . ⁧آل⁩ (with the madda, the family of, the family of), stands before the name of a forefather to indicate a family or dynasty: ⁧آل مَنْصُور⁩ The family Manṣūr». It is written as a separate word and is common in the names of the Gulf. It should not be confused with the article ⁧الـ⁩ , which attaches itself to the word: ⁧المَنْصُورِيّ⁩ « al-Manṣūrī». In Latin spelling, both become often "Al" or "Al" or "El" (ONO-)02). 6. Composite names and word names Names ⁧عَبْد⁩ . ⁧عَبْد⁩ "Servant" + one of God's names forms one name only: ⁧عَبْد الله⁩ , ⁧عَبْد الرَّحْمٰن⁩ , ⁧عَبْد الكَرِيم⁩ , ⁧عَبْد القَادِر⁩ , ⁧عَبْد العَزِيز⁩ . It is written in two words but it is a single name: you can not call the personʿAbd"Son" (meaning "servant of the..." ), or divide the name between two boxes of a form. In the pronunciation, the article is similar to the solar letters: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān. Names ⁧الدِّين⁩ . Name + ⁧الدِّين⁩ Religion's: ⁧نُور الدِّين⁩ "Light of the Faith" ⁧صَلَاح الدِّين⁩ , ⁧عِزّ الدِّين⁩ , ⁧خَيْر الدِّين⁩ . That's one name, too. Other compounds. Some female names are composed: ⁧فَاطِمَة الزَّهْرَاء⁩ , ⁧نُور الهُدَى⁩ . Some male names have two fixed parts: ⁧مُحَمَّد أَمِين⁩ , ⁧مُحَمَّد عَلِيّ⁩ (in Egypt and the Maghreb), which are sometimes a single name and sometimes name + father's name: only the document says so. Names that are words. Many names are adjectives or common names you know: ⁧كَرِيم⁩ "Bountiful' is the name of the family. ⁧سَعِيد⁩ Happy, ⁧جَمِيلَة⁩ "Beautiful" ⁧أَمَل⁩ "Hope" is the word "hope," ⁧نُور⁩ Lights, lamps and lighting fittings ⁧هُدَى⁩ • the straight way • ⁧أَمِين⁩ "Trusted' ⁧حَسَن⁩ - Good, good. In an unvocalized text, therefore, ⁧سعيد⁩ can be a name or adjective: it decides the context. Male or female? Names in ⁧ة⁩ are usually feminine ( ⁧فَاطِمَة⁩ , ⁧جَمِيلَة⁩ ), but some male names end up in ⁧ة⁩ : ⁧حَمْزَة⁩ , ⁧أُسَامَة⁩ , ⁧طَلْحَة⁩ . Many female names do not have ⁧ة⁩ : ⁧زَيْنَب⁩ , ⁧مَرْيَم⁩ , ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ , ⁧هُدَى⁩ . ⁧نُور⁩ is both male and female. 7. The name in documents The picture is simplified: within each country there are many exceptions, and it is always worth reading the boxes of document one by one. Area Typical form of official name Gulf, Iraq chain: name + father's name + grandfather's name + family or tribe's name ( ⁧الاِسْمُ⁩ ⁧الرُّبَاعِيّ⁩ ) Egypt, Sudan chain: name + father's name + grandfather's name (+ great-grandfather); many families do not have a fixed surname, and in the passport the last element is to be ... title: Transliteration and variants
text: Lesson overview ⁧مُحَمَّد⁩ you can find written Muḥammad, Muhammad, Mohammed, Mohammad, Mohamed; ⁧يُوسُف⁩ becomes Yusuf, Youssef, Yousef, Youcef. They are not mistakes: every country and every European language has its own habits, and none is official for all. In this unit you learn the most common Latin spellings (English, French, Egyptian), their reasons, and above all the method of going back from Latin to Arabic: what Arabic letters can be behind a Latin letter, where are the ambiguities, when you have to ask. You also learn to spell a name in Arabic. A week. Item Details Code ONO-02 Level A2 · Onomastic trace Prerequisites ONO-01 exceeded; name of the letters (L0) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 71 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (Tag ONO-02), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. explain why the same name has many Latin spells; 2. read the most common English, French and Egyptian spellings and connect them to Arabic letters; 3. Reduce a Latin spelling to the possible Arabic forms, recognizing ambiguities (Hassan: ⁧حَسَن⁩ or ⁧حَسَّان⁩ ?); 4. recognizing the Arabizi of messages (3 = ⁧ع⁩ , 7 = ⁧ح⁩ ); 5. spell a name in Arabic and understand a spelling dictation. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: because so many graphs · section 3: the consonants · exercise 1 2 Section 4: vowels, article, double · section 5: national traditions · exercises 2–3 · vocabulary 3 Sections 6–7: arabizi · from Latin to Arabic · exercises 4–5 4 Sections 8–9: documents · spelling · reading · exercise 7 5 Listening: dictation of names (exercise 9) · writing (exercise 8) 6 Tutor session: spelling a name 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Why so many graphs 1. There is no single system. Scholars use precise systems with diacritical signs (in this DIN course 31635: Muḥammad, ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān); documents and everyday life use simple, unmarked graphs. 2. Two European traditions. In the countries related to English (Golfo, Iraq, Jordan, Egypt in part) it is written "English" (sh, j, oo, ee); in the countries related to French (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Lebanon in part) (ch, dj, ou). 3. title: Related pronouns
text: Lesson overview The man who wears the glasses is the one who lost the bag, the colleague with whom I work.The person who arrives late signs the register.Then you describe people and things without repeating the name. In Arabic the relative pronoun ( ⁧الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ ...) is used only after a given name and agrees with him; Inside its, when the name is not the subject, a pronoun of recovery recalls it ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ , letter. The book that I read it. After an indeterminate name its is not: ⁧كِتَابٌ قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ It's a book I read. Completing the Unit ⁧مَنْ⁩ ... ⁧مَا⁩ It's what it is. The context is the description of people and objects (announcements of lost property) and then work in an office. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-13 Level A2 · Module A2.3 Complex frasi and irregular verbs Prerequisites Trace ONO exceeded; suffix pronouns (A2-10); dual and plural (A1, A2-08) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 72–73 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-13), script for speech synthesis, photos of people to describe, session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. Choose the right relative pronoun by gender and number (recognizing duals and plural female); 2. use the resume pronoun as an object complement, after a preposition and to say "whose" is; 3. build its without pronoun after an indeterminate name; 4. use ⁧مَنْ⁩ • who, the one who is ⁧مَا⁩ • what it is, including ⁧كُلُّ مَا⁩ • all that is done; 5. describe people and objects, understand a lost object ad and the rules of an office. Texts. Dialogues and examples are given; the readings of the module A2.3 are partially vocalized (vowels on new words and where reading is ambiguous). Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · Who is that gentleman? Saturday night, at the festival of the Italian-Arab association. Luca and Hudā They look at the guests. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَنِ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي يَلْبَسُ القَمِيصَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧الأَزْرَقَ؟⁩ Lūkā: mani r-raǧulu llaḏī yalbasu l- qamīṣa l-azraq? Luke: Who is the man wearing the blue shirt? ⁧هُوَ مُحَمَّد السَّيِّد، صَدِيقُ أَبِي، الَّذِي⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧كَتَبْنَا اسْمَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي القَائِمَةِ!⁩ Hudā: huwa Muḥammad as-Sayyid, ṣadīqu abī, allaḏī katabnā smahu marratayni fī l-qāʾima! Hudā: È Muḥammad As-Sayyid, my father's friend, the one whose name we wrote twice on the list! ⁧وَالمَرْأَةُ الَّتِي تَتَكَلَّمُ مَعَهُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-l-marʾatu llatī tatakallamu maʿah? What about the woman who talks to him? ⁧زَوْجَتُهُ. هِيَ الَّتِي طَبَخَتْ كُلَّ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧الحَلَوِيَّاتِ الَّتِي عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ.⁩ Hudā: zawǧatuh. hiya llatī ṭabaḫat kulla l-ḥalawiyyāti llatī ʿalā ṭ-ṭāwila. Hudā: His wife. She's the one who made all the desserts on the table. ⁧وَالشَّابَّانِ اللَّذَانِ يَقِفَانِ عِنْدَ البَابِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-š-šābbāni llaḏāni yaqifāni ʿinda l-bāb? What about the two guys standing by the door? ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُهُمَا. رُبَّمَا هُمَا الطَّالِبَانِ اللَّذَانِ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧دَعَاهُمَا بَاوْلُو.⁩ Hudā: lā aʿrifuhumā. rubbamā humā ṭ- ṭālibāni llaḏāni daʿāhumā Bāwlū. HudāI don't know them. Maybe it's the two students who invited Paul. ⁧وَالسَّيِّدَةُ الَّتِي سَلَّمْتِ عَلَيْهَا قَبْلَ قَلِيلٍ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-s-sayyidatu llatī sallamti ʿalayhā qabla qalīl? Luca: And the lady you said goodbye to earlier? ⁧هِيَ أُمّ كَرِيم، جَارَةُ سَلْمَى فِي⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧القَاهِرَةِ. جَاءَتْ تَزُورُ ابْنَهَا الَّذِي يَدْرُسُ هُنَا.⁩ Hudā: hiya Umm Karīm, ǧāratu Salmā fī l-qāhira. ǧāʾat tazūru bnahā llaḏī yadrusu hunā. Hudā: It's Umm Karīm, the neighbour of Salmā Cairo. She came to see her son, who studies here. ⁧كُلُّ مَنْ فِي هٰذِهِ الغُرْفَةِ يَعْرِفُ سَلْمَى!⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: kullu man fī hāḏihi l-ġurfati yaʿrifu Salmā! Luke: Everyone in this room knows Salmā! ⁧طَبْعًا. وَمَنْ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا يَسْمَعُ عَنْهَا بَعْدَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧خَمْسِ دَقَائِقَ!⁩ Hudā: ṭabʿan. wa-man lā yaʿrifuhā yasmaʿu ʿanhā baʿda ḫamsi daqāʾiq! Hudā: Sure. And those who don't know her hear about her after five minutes! What to notice. ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧المَرْأَةُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الشَّابَّانِ اللَّذَانِ⁩ : the relative pronoun follows a definite noun and agrees with it. The subject is not repeated in the relative ( ⁧الَّذِي يَلْبَسُ⁩ ), but the complement yes, with a suffix: ⁧الطَّالِبَانِ اللَّذَانِ دَعَاهُمَا بَاوْلُو⁩ □ the two students Paul invited (Lett. who invited them) ⁧السَّيِّدَةُ الَّتِي سَلَّمْتِ عَلَيْهَا⁩ The lady you greeted (Lett. on her) ⁧الحَلَوِيَّاتُ الَّتِي عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ : its can be without verb. ⁧كُلُّ مَنْ⁩ • all those who are entitled, ⁧مَنْ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا⁩ (section) 5). ⁧رُبَّمَا⁩ Maybe it is. ⁧حَلَوِيَّات⁩ Sweets. In this scene Umm Karīm is the neighbour of Salmā in Cairo, known in ONO-01: no connection with the colleague Karīm. 2. Related pronouns  Singular Dual Plural Masculine  ⁧اللَّذَانِالَّذِي⁩ ⁧الَّذِينَاللَّذَيْنِ⁩ / (people) Feminine  ⁧اللَّتَانِالَّتِي⁩ ⁧اللَّوَاتِياللَّتَيْنِ⁩ / , ⁧اللَّاتِي⁩ (people) 1. Agreement. Its name takes the genre and number to which it refers: ⁧الوَلَدُ الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧البِنْتُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الطُّلَّابُ الَّذِينَ⁩ . 2. Plural of Things = ⁧الَّتِي⁩ . As with adjectives (A2-08): ⁧الكُتُبُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ الَّتِي⁩ . 3. The dual has two forms, such as the name: ⁧اللَّذَانِ⁩ the name, ⁧اللَّذَيْنِ⁩ to the parent and the accusative ( ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَيْنِ⁩ ⁧اللَّذَيْنِ⁩ …). The other forms do not decline. 4. The Plural Female ⁧اللَّوَاتِي⁩ / ⁧اللَّاتِي⁩ meets in the formal texts; many use ⁧الَّتِي⁩ also for women at Plural. Recognize him; Writing is okay too ⁧الَّتِي⁩ . 5. Graffia. ⁧الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ they are written with only one lam and shadda; the duals and ⁧اللَّوَاتِي⁩ with two lam . Only after a given name. Its Arabic is actually an adjective with the article: it is used when the name has the article, a suffix or is a proper name ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي⁩ …, ⁧كِتَابِي الَّذِي⁩ …, ⁧سَلْمَى الَّتِي⁩ …). After an indeterminate name it is not used (section 4). Unnamed. Its may be by itself: ⁧الَّذِي يَعْمَلُ هُنَا⁩ "The one who works here" ⁧هِيَ الَّتِي طَبَخَتْ⁩ She's the one who cooked. It's the Arabic way of saying "it's him who..." she's the one who... 3. The pronoun for recovery Inside its, the name to which it refers is called by a pronoun ( ⁧عَائِد⁩ (a) which returns to the person, except when he is the subject. Function in its Example Lett. Translation Subject: No recovery ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي يَعْمَلُ⁩ ⁧مَعِي⁩ The man who works with me The man who works with me object complement: suffix on the verb ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ the book that I read it the book I read after a preposition: suffix on the preposition ⁧البَيْتُ الَّذِي أَسْكُنُ⁩ ⁧فِيهِ⁩ the house that I live in it the house where I live  ⁧الزَّمِيلَةُ الَّتِي أَعْمَلُ⁩ ⁧مَعَهَا⁩ I work with her. my colleague with whom I work possessive: suffix on the name ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي⁩ ⁧سَيَّارَتُهُ حَمْرَاءُ⁩ the man that his car is red The man whose car is red  ⁧الطَّالِبَةُ الَّتِي نَسِيتُ⁩ ⁧اسْمَهَا⁩ The student I forgot her name The student whose name I forgot Four comments: 1. The verb of its accords with its subject, which is not necessarily the starting name: ⁧الكُتُبُ الَّتِي⁩ ⁧اشْتَرَاهَا أَبِي⁩ The books that my father bought (the subject is ⁧أَبِي⁩ ). 2. The subject-matter of the recovery is sometimes omitted in the formal writing ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُ⁩ ). You always wear it. 3. Place and time. Where and when the relevant information is made by: ⁧فِيهِ⁩ / ⁧فِيهَا⁩ : ⁧المَدِينَةُ الَّتِي وُلِدْتُ فِيهَا⁩ The city in which I was born in New York, ⁧اليَوْمُ الَّذِي وَصَلْنَا فِيهِ⁩ The day we arrived. 4. Verbs with preposition (A2-10): the preposition remains in the relative with the suffix: ⁧الرَّقْمُ الَّذِي اتَّصَلْتُ بِهِ⁩ On number I called, ⁧الشَّخْصُ الَّذِي أَبْحَثُ عَنْهُ⁩ The person I'm looking for. 4. Its after an indeterminate name After an indeterminate name its follows the name without relative pronoun, as an adjective. The recovery stays. Determined Indeterminate  ⁧رَجُلٌ يَلْبَسُ نَظَّارَةًالرَّجُلُ الَّذِي يَلْبَسُ نَظَّارَةً⁩ the man wearing glasses a man wearing glasses  ⁧كِتَابٌ قَرَأْتُهُالكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ the book I read a book I read ⁧الشَّقَّةُ الَّتِي نَسْكُنُ فِيهَا⁩ ⁧شَقَّةٌ نَسْكُنُ فِيهَا⁩ the apartment we live in an apartment where we live It is a very frequent construction in ads and news: ⁧مَطْلُوبٌ مُتَرْجِمٌ يَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ⁩ • Seek interpreter who speaks Arabic • ⁧رَأَيْتُ امْرَأَةً تَبْكِي⁩ I saw a woman crying. The first clue that tells you here begins a relative ' is an indeterminate name followed by a verb immediately. Watch your senses. A frequent mistake is to put ⁧الَّذِي⁩ after an indefinite name ( ⁧رَجُلٌ الَّذِي⁩ ...): it's wrong. And a phrase like ⁧عِنْدِي صَدِيقٌ يَسْكُنُ فِي رُومَا⁩ means "I have a friend who lives in Rome."He doesn't have a friend, he lives in Rome. 5. ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧مَا⁩ related Related Meaning Example Translation ⁧مَنْ⁩ who, who, those who (people) ⁧مَنْ يَتَأَخَّرُ يَكْتُبُ اسْمَهُ فِي⁩ ⁧السِّجِلِّ.⁩ Whoever arrives late writes the name in the register. ⁧مَا⁩ what, what (things) ⁧لَا أَفْهَمُ مَا تَقُولُ.⁩ I don't understand what you're saying. ⁧كُلُّ مَنْ⁩ all those ⁧كُلُّ مَنْ يَعْمَلُ هُنَا يَعْرِفُهُ.⁩ Everyone who works here knows him. ⁧كُلُّ مَا⁩ all that ⁧كُلُّ مَا قَالَهُ صَحِيحٌ.⁩ Everything he said is true. 1. ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧مَا⁩ they do not have a name in front of them: they already contain "he" and "he." 2. The verb after ⁧مَنْ⁩ is usually to the singular male, although the sense is plural: ⁧مَنْ يُرِيدُ⁩ ... who wants, those who want to. 3. With prepositions ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧مَا⁩ they melt: ⁧مِنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ → ⁧مِمَّا⁩ From what it does, ⁧عَنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ → ⁧عَمَّا⁩ • of what it is that it does, ⁧مِنْ⁩ + ⁧مَنْ⁩ → ⁧مِمَّنْ⁩ "Who's "Who': ⁧سَأَلَنِي عَمَّا حَدَثَ⁩ He asked me what happened. To be recognized. 4. Do not confuse ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧مَا⁩ related to applications ⁧مَنْ؟⁩ "Who?" and ⁧مَا؟⁩ - what? ⁧مَا⁩ with ⁧مَا⁩ of Denial ( ⁧مَا ذَهَبْتُ⁩ I didn't go. It decides the structure of the sentence. 6. Dialogue 2 · The first day Monday morning at the police station. Sāra accompany Nādya, a new interpreter, on his first day of work. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧هٰذَا هُوَ المَكْتَبُ الَّذِي سَتَعْمَلِينَ فِيهِ.⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧المَكْتَبُ الَّذِي بِجَانِبِهِ لِكَرِيم.⁩ Sāra: hāḏā huwa l-maktabu llaḏī sa- taʿmalīna fīh. al-maktabu llaḏī bi- ǧānibihi li-Karīm. Sāra: This is the office where you will work. The next one is from Karīm. ⁧وَالزَّمِيلَتَانِ اللَّتَانِ تَجْلِسَانِ هُنَاكَ؟⁩ : ⁧نَادْيَة⁩ Nādya: wa-z-zamīlatāni llatāni taǧlisāni hunāk? Nādya: And the two colleagues who are sitting there? ⁧هُمَا مِنْ مَكْتَبِ الاِسْتِقْبَالِ. هُمَا اللَّتَانِ⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ ⁧تَسْتَقْبِلَانِ المُرَاجِعِينَ الأَجَانِبَ وَتَتَّصِلَانِ بِنَا.⁩ Sāra: humā min maktabi l-istiqbāl. humā llatāni tastaqbilāni l-murāǧiʿīna l- aǧānib wa-tattaṣilāni binā. Sāra: I am of acceptance. They are the ones who receive foreign users and call us. ⁧هَلْ هُنَاكَ قَوَاعِدُ يَجِبُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَهَا؟⁩ : ⁧نَادْيَة⁩ Nādya: hal hunāka qawāʿidu yaǧibu an aʿrifahā? Typical errors Error Correction ⁧رَجُلٌ يَبْكِيرَجُلٌ الَّذِي يَبْكِي⁩ : after an indefinite name nothing relative ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُ⁩ (without resumption) ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ ⁧المَدِينَةُ الَّتِي أَسْكُنُ⁩ ⁧المَدِينَةُ الَّتِي أَسْكُنُ فِيهَا⁩ ⁧الكُتُبُ الَّتِيالكُتُبُ الَّذِينَ⁩ : plural of things = female singular  • whose name is suffixed ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي سَيَّارَتُهُ حَمْرَاءُ:الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي سَيَّارَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ⁩  ⁧الطَّالِبَانِ اللَّذَانِالطَّالِبَانِ الَّذِي⁩ write ⁧اللذي⁩ with two lam ⁧الَّذِي⁩ (a lam), but ⁧اللَّذَانِ⁩ (two) ⁧مَنْ يَتَأَخَّرُمَنْ يَتَأَخَّرُونَ⁩ : after ⁧مَنْ⁩ the verb is usually singular 16. Flashcard Deck A2, tag A2-13: 30 rumors. Also prepare a series of cards     ♪ Unify sentences ♪ (in front of two sentences, behind the sentence with its and shooting) and five cards for ⁧مِمَّا⁩ , ⁧عَمَّا⁩ , ⁧مِمَّنْ⁩ . 17. title: The subordinates: why, why, when, if
text: Lesson overview I think it's a good idea.I go because they invited me, when I arrive I call you, if you lose, ask for it, before I leave, while I studied, .................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... In this unit you learn to distinguish ⁧أَنَّ⁩ ( + sentence) from ⁧أَنْ⁩ ( + verb to conjunctiva), to give a cause with ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ , to place the shares in time with ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ , ⁧قَبْلَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَعْدَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَمَا⁩ , and to make a real hypothesis with ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect. The context is the choice of travel to Cairo and practical advice before leaving. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-14 Level A2 · Module A2.3 Complex frasi and irregular verbs Prerequisites A2-13 exceeded; conjunctive and ⁧أَنْ⁩ ( A2-04); Junior (A2-05); suffix pronouns (A2-10) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 74–75 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-14), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. distinguish ⁧أَنَّ⁩ + sentence (facts, opinions) from ⁧أَنْ⁩ + conjunctive (will, necessity, possibility); 2. use ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ with the subject to the prosecution or with a suffix pronoun ( ⁧أَنَّهُ⁩ , ⁧لِأَنَّنِي⁩ ); 3. say "when" with ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ (and recognize ⁧لَمَّا⁩ , ⁧حِينَ⁩ ); 4. build a real condition with ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect and the ⁧فَـ⁩ in the second part, also the negative ( ⁧إِذَا لَمْ⁩ …); 5. sort the shares with ⁧قَبْلَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَعْدَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَمَا⁩ , ⁧لِذٰلِكَ⁩ ; 6. motivate a choice, express an opinion, give advice and instructions with conditions. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧أَنْ⁩ · financial years 1–2 2 Section 3: ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ and the cause · exercise 3 · lexicon (first half) 3 Section 4: ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ , ⁧لَمَّا⁩ , ⁧حِينَ⁩ · year 4 4 Reading 1: an interview · exercise 11 5 Script B: Why? · writing: explain a choice (exercise 13) 6 Oral production: reasons 7 Anki · review 8 Dialogue 2 · section 5: ⁧إِذَا⁩ · year 5 9 Section 6: ⁧قَبْلَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَعْدَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَمَا⁩ , ⁧لِذٰلِكَ⁩ · year 6 · lexicon (second half) 10 Exercises 7–10 11 Reading 2: instructions with conditions · operation 12 12 Script C · writing: argumentative text (exercise 14) 13 Session with the tutor: real hypotheses 14 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · Why Cairo? Coffee break at the police station. Karīm He heard about Luca's trip. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧سَمِعْتُ أَنَّكَ سَتُسَافِرُ إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ فِي⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧يُولْيُو. لِمَاذَا القَاهِرَةُ، وَلَيْسَ فَاس؟⁩ Karīm: samiʿtu annaka sa-tusāfiru ilā l- qāhirati fī Yūlyū. li-māḏā l-qāhira, wa- laysa Fās? Karīm: I heard you're going to Cairo in July. Why Cairo and not Fès? ⁧لِأَنَّ سَلْمَى دَعَتْنِي، وَلِأَنَّ ابْنَ عَمِّهَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧يَعْمَلُ فِي مَرْكَزٍ لِلُّغَاتِ هُنَاكَ.⁩ Lūkā: li-anna Salmā daʿatnī, wa-li-anna bna ʿammihā yaʿmalu fī markazin li-l- luġāti hunāk. Luke: Because he invited me Salmā, and because his cousin works in a language center there. ⁧لٰكِنِّي أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ فَاسَ أَجْمَلُ!⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: lākinnī aʿtaqidu anna Fāsa aǧmal! Karīm: But I think Fès is more beautiful! ⁧رُبَّمَا. لٰكِنِّي قَرَّرْتُ أَنْ أَبْدَأَ بِالقَاهِرَةِ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧عِنْدَمَا أَرْجِعُ، سَأُفَكِّرُ فِي رِحْلَةٍ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ.⁩ Lūkā: rubbamā. lākinnī qarrartu an abdaʾa bi-l-qāhira. ʿindamā arǧiʿu, sa- ufakkiru fī riḥlatin ilā l-maġrib. Maybe. But I decided to start with Cairo. When I get back, I'll think of a trip to Morocco. ⁧وَهَلْ تَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ سَتَفْهَمُ المِصْرِيِّينَ؟⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: wa-hal taẓunnu annaka sa- tafhamu l-miṣriyyīn? Karīm: And you think you understand the Egyptians? ⁧لَسْتُ مُتَأَكِّدًا. أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ لَهْجَتَهُمْ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧مُخْتَلِفَةٌ عَنِ الفُصْحَى، لٰكِنَّ سَلْمَى تَقُولُ إِنَّ⁩ ⁧النَّاسَ هُنَاكَ يَفْهَمُونَ الفُصْحَى جَيِّدًا.⁩ Lūkā: lastu mutaʾakkidan. aʿrifu anna lahǧatahum muḫtalifatun ʿani l-fuṣḥā, lākinna Salmā taqūlu inna n-nāsa hunāka yafhamūna l-fuṣḥā ǧayyidā. I'm not sure. I know their dialect is different from the standard Arabic, but Salmā He says people there understand the standard well. ⁧هٰذَا صَحِيحٌ. وَلِأَنَّ الأَفْلَامَ المِصْرِيَّةَ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧مَشْهُورَةٌ جِدًّا، النَّاسُ فِي كُلِّ البِلَادِ العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ ⁧تَقْرِيبًا يَفْهَمُونَ المِصْرِيَّةَ.⁩ Karīm: hāḏā ṣaḥīḥ. wa-li-anna l-aflāma l-miṣriyyata mašhūratun ǧiddan, an- nāsu fī kulli l-bilādi l-ʿarabiyyati taqrīban yafhamūna l-miṣriyya. Karīm: It's true. And since Egyptian films are very famous, people in almost all Arab countries understand Egyptian. ⁧وَأَنْتَ، مَتَى زُرْتَ القَاهِرَةَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-anta, matā zurta l-qāhira? Luca: And you, when were you in Cairo? ⁧لَمَّا كُنْتُ طَالِبًا. أَتَذَكَّرُ أَنَّنِي ضِعْتُ فِي⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ، لِأَنَّ كُلَّ الشَّوَارِعِ كَانَتْ تُشْبِهُ⁩ ⁧بَعْضَهَا!⁩ Karīm: lammā kuntu ṭāliban. ataḏakkaru annanī ḍiʿtu fī l-yawmi l- awwal, li-anna kulla š-šawāriʿi kānat tušbihu baʿḍahā! KarīmWhen I was a student. I remember the first day I got lost, because all the roads looked alike! ⁧لِذٰلِكَ سَأَشْتَرِي خَرِيطَةً قَبْلَ أَنْ أُسَافِرَ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: li-ḏālika sa-aštarī ḫarīṭatan qabla an usāfir. Luca: That's why I'll buy a map before I leave. Karīm: ḫarīṭa?! ʿindaka hātifun yā Lūkā! Karīm: A map?! You have the phone. ⁧خَرِيطَة؟! عِنْدَكَ هَاتِفٌ يَا لُوكَا!⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Luca! What to notice. ⁧سَمِعْتُ أَنَّكَ سَتُسَافِرُ⁩ , ⁧أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ فَاسَ أَجْمَلُ⁩ , ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ لَهْجَتَهُمْ⁩ ...: after the verbs of knowing, hearing, believing comes ⁧أَنَّ⁩ + sentence; the following subject: ⁧أَنَّ⁩ goes to the accusative ( ⁧لَهْجَتَهُمْ⁩ , ⁧فَاسَ⁩ ) or is a suffix ( ⁧أَنَّكَ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّنِي⁩ ). Instead of ⁧قَرَّرْتُ أَنْ أَبْدَأَ⁩ : after decision is taken ⁧أَنْ⁩ + conjunctive (A2-04). ⁧تَقُولُ إِنَّ⁩ : after ... say... is used ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ( A2-19). ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ • because it is not, ⁧عِنْدَمَا أَرْجِعُ⁩ When I return to my place (with the imperfect, for the future), ⁧لَمَّا كُنْتُ⁩ - when I was a girl, ⁧قَبْلَ أَنْ أُسَافِرَ⁩ • before leaving • • ⁧لِذٰلِكَ⁩ For this reason. ⁧الفُصْحَى⁩ • Standard Arabic. ⁧تُشْبِهُ بَعْضَهَا⁩ They were similar (to each other) to each other. ⁧ضِعْتُ⁩ I've lost my way (from ⁧ضَاعَ⁩ , concave: A2-15). That the Egyptian dialect is understood in almost all the Arab world is opinion of Karīm, very popular and linked to Egyptian cinema and television. 2. ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧أَنْ⁩  ⁧أَنْ⁩ (an) ⁧أَنَّ⁩ (Anna) After verbs of will, necessity, possibility: ⁧أُرِيدُ⁩ , ⁧يَجِبُ⁩ , ⁧يُمْكِنُ⁩ , ⁧أَسْتَطِيعُ⁩ , ⁧قَرَّرَ⁩ , ⁧طَلَبَ⁩ verbs of knowledge, opinion, perception: ⁧أَعْرِفُ⁩ , ⁧عَرَفْتُ⁩ , ⁧سَمِعْتُ⁩ , ⁧أَعْتَقِدُ⁩ , ⁧أَظُنُّ⁩ , ⁧رَأَيْتُ⁩ , ⁧أَتَذَكَّرُ⁩ Following a verb to the conjunctive a sentence: name or suffix + predicate Example ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَافِرَ.⁩ ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ السَّفَرَ غَالٍ.⁩ Translation I want to go. I know the trip is expensive. The Next Subject ⁧أَنَّ⁩ . ⁧أَنَّ⁩ immediately after him wants a name to the accusative or a pronoun suffix, never directly a verb: Phrase With ⁧أَنَّ⁩ Translation ⁧الدَّرْسُ صَعْبٌ.⁩ ⁧أَظُنُّ أَنَّ الدَّرْسَ صَعْبٌ.⁩ I think the lesson is hard. ⁧سَلْمَى مِصْرِيَّةٌ.⁩ ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ سَلْمَى مِصْرِيَّةٌ.⁩ I know that Salmā She's Egyptian. ⁧هُوَ وَصَلَ.⁩ ⁧سَمِعْتُ أَنَّهُ وَصَلَ.⁩ I heard he's here. ⁧أَنَا مَرِيضٌ.⁩ ⁧يَعْرِفُ أَنَّنِي مَرِيضٌ.⁩ He knows I'm sick. The forms with the suffixes: ⁧أَنَّنِي⁩ / ⁧أَنِّي⁩ , ⁧أَنَّكَ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّكِ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّهُ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّهَا⁩ , ⁧أَنَّنَا⁩ , ⁧أَنَّكُمْ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّهُمْ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّهُنَّ⁩ . When the phrase begins with a verb, the suffix is used ⁧أَنَّهُ⁩ It's that he or the neutral suffix. ⁧ـهُ⁩ : ⁧سَمِعْتُ أَنَّهُ سَيُغْلَقُ المَكْتَبُ⁩ I have heard that the office will be closed (to be recognized). No vowels ⁧أن⁩ The same is written in the two cases: decides what follows. If after ⁧أن⁩ comes a verb to the imperfect, is ⁧أَنْ⁩ ; if a name or suffix comes, it is ⁧أَنَّ⁩ . The Italian conjunctive. I think it's in Arabic after ⁧أَنَّ⁩ the verb remains at the sign. The Arab conjunctive (A2-04) is only used after ⁧أَنْ⁩ , ⁧لَنْ⁩ , ⁧لِكَيْ⁩ , ⁧حَتَّى⁩ . 3. ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ and the cause Construction Example Translation ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ + name of the accused person ⁧لِأَنَّ الطَّقْسَ جَمِيلٌ⁩ because time is beautiful ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ + suffix ⁧لِأَنَّنِي تَعِبْتُ⁩ · ⁧لِأَنَّهُ مَرِيضٌ⁩ because he is sick · because I am tired ⁧بِسَبَبِ⁩ + name ⁧بِسَبَبِ المَطَرِ⁩ because of the rain ⁧لِـ⁩ / ⁧لِكَيْ⁩ + conjunctive (purpose, A2-04) ⁧جِئْتُ لِأَتَعَلَّمَ⁩ I came to learn Why? Why... ⁧لِمَاذَا⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ — ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ ... Be careful not to confuse the cause ( ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ + sentence: ... because it is so) with purpose ( ⁧لِـ⁩ / ⁧لِكَيْ⁩ + conjunctive: Other words of the cause to be recognized: ⁧بِمَا أَنَّ⁩ • since it is not ⁧إِذْ⁩ • because it is formal; ⁧وَذٰلِكَ لِأَنَّ⁩ This is because it is (in the news). 4. When: ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ , ⁧لَمَّا⁩ , ⁧حِينَ⁩ Joint With Example Translation ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ perfect (passed) ⁧عِنْدَمَا وَصَلْتُ، اتَّصَلْتُ بِكَ.⁩ When I got here, I called you. ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ imperfect (habitation or future) ⁧عِنْدَمَا أَصِلُ، سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ.⁩ When I arrive (I will) I call you. ⁧لَمَّا⁩ perfect (only past) ⁧لَمَّا رَآنِي، ابْتَسَمَ.⁩ When he saw me, he smiled. ⁧حِينَمَا⁩ , ⁧حِينَ⁩ as ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ (formal) … ⁧حِينَ بَدَأَتِ الحَرْبُ⁩ When the war began... Two ⁧لَمَّا⁩ . ⁧لَمَّا⁩ + Perfect = when (past); ⁧لَمَّا⁩ + Jussive = not yet (A2-05): ⁧لَمَّا يَصِلْ⁩ It's not here yet. Look at the form of the verb. When is it? ⁧مَتَى؟⁩ is the application; ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ introduces a sentence: ⁧مَتَى تَصِلُ؟⁩ — ⁧عِنْدَمَا يَنْتَهِي العَمَلُ⁩ When do you get here? When the job is finished 5. The actual  is: ⁧إِذَا⁩ ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect, even when the meaning is present or future: ⁧إِذَا وَصَلْتَ مُتَأَخِّرًا⁩ If you're late, it's too late. The second part may be: Part Two Example Translation perfect (formal style) ⁧إِذَا دَرَسْتَ نَجَحْتَ.⁩ If you study, pass. imperfect ⁧إِذَا تَأَخَّرَ القِطَارُ نَنْتَظِرُ.⁩ If the train is late, we wait. ⁧فَـ⁩ + imperative ⁧إِذَا ضِعْتَ فَاسْأَلْ شُرْطِيًّا.⁩ If you get lost, ask a cop. ⁧لَنْ⁩ / ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ / ⁧سَـ⁩ + ⁧فَـ⁩ ⁧إِذَا جَاءَ فَسَأُخْبِرُكَ.⁩ If he comes, I'll tell you. ⁧فَـ⁩ + nominal sentence ⁧إِذَا كَانَ عِنْدَكَ وَقْتٌ فَالمَتْحَفُ قَرِيبٌ.⁩ If you have time, the museum is close. ⁧فَـ⁩ + ⁧لَا⁩ + legal (prohibited) ⁧إِذَا كُنْتَ مَرِيضًا فَلَا تَأْتِ.⁩ If you're sick, don't come. The ⁧فَـ⁩ . It is placed in front of the second part when it does not start with a perfect or simple imperfect: imperative, prohibition, ⁧سَـ⁩ / ⁧سَوْفَ⁩ , ⁧لَنْ⁩ , ⁧قَدْ⁩ , nominal sentence. It translates to a comma. If not. ⁧إِذَا لَمْ⁩ + Judging: ⁧إِذَا لَمْ تَفْهَمْ فَاسْأَلْ⁩ If you don't understand, ask for it. title: Weak verbs in all times
text: Lesson overview Many of the most frequent verbs have in the root a ⁧و⁩ or a ⁧ي⁩ : ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ • arrive • • ⁧قَالَ⁩ "Simple' means: ⁧بَاعَ⁩ "Sell" is the name of the manufacturer. ⁧مَشَى⁩ "walking" is the term "walking," ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ Forget about it. You've met them time by time (A2-02 → A2-06); in this unit you put them in line at all times and ways, with summary tables, and learn the few rules that explain all forms: ⁧و⁩ which falls into the assimilated, the long vowel that shortens in the concave, the final vowel that changes or falls into the defective. The context is the story: a tourist who lost his passport, a weekend in the mountains, a news. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-15 Level A2 · Module A2.3 Complex frasi and irregular verbs Prerequisites A2-14 exceeded; perfect, imperfect, conjunctive, juxtaposed and imperative (A2-02 → A2-06) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 76–77 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-15), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the three types of weak verb from the root: assimilated ( ⁧و⁩ at the beginning), concave ( ⁧و⁩ / ⁧ي⁩ in the middle), defective ( ⁧و⁩ / ⁧ي⁩ at the end); 2. combine in all times and ways ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ , ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧بَاعَ⁩ , ⁧خَافَ⁩ , ⁧دَعَا⁩ , ⁧مَشَى⁩ , ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ and the verbs that follow the same models; 3. forming participles and maṣdar the most frequent weak verbs ( ⁧قَائِل⁩ , ⁧مَاشٍ⁩ , ⁧وُصُول⁩ , ⁧نِسْيَان⁩ ); 4. Rediscover the root of a short form ( ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ , ⁧صِلْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَنْسَ⁩ , ⁧اِمْشِ⁩ ); 5. tell facts to the past and understand news with many weak verbs. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · The lost passport Commissioner, door. A Moroccan tourist (invented) lost his passport. Karīm translates, Luca asks the questions. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَتَى وَصَلْتَ إِلَى مِيلَانُو؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: matā waṣalta ilā Mīlānū? Luca: When did you arrive in Milan? ⁧وَصَلْتُ أَوَّلَ أَمْسِ مَعَ زَوْجَتِي. نَزَلْنَا⁩ : ⁧السَّائِح⁩ ⁧فِي فُنْدُقٍ قُرْبَ المَحَطَّةِ.⁩ as-sāʾiḥ: waṣaltu awwala amsi maʿa zawǧatī. nazalnā fī funduqin qurba l- maḥaṭṭa. Tourist: I arrived the day before yesterday with my wife. We went down to a hotel near the station. ⁧وَأَيْنَ وَضَعْتَ جَوَازَ السَّفَرِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-ayna waḍaʿta ǧawāza s- safar? And where did you put your passport? ⁧وَضَعْتُهُ فِي حَقِيبَةِ الظَّهْرِ. هٰذَا⁩ : ⁧السَّائِح⁩ ⁧الصَّبَاحَ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُغَيِّرَ مَالًا، فَلَمْ أَجِدْهُ.⁩ as-sāʾiḥ: waḍaʿtuhu fī ḥaqībati ẓ-ẓahr. hāḏā ṣ-ṣabāḥa aradtu an uġayyira mālan, fa-lam aǧidh. I put it in my backpack. I wanted to change some money this morning, and I didn't find it. ⁧هَلْ نِمْتُمْ فِي الفُنْدُقِ كُلَّ اللَّيْلِ، أَمْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧خَرَجْتُمْ؟⁩ Karīm: hal nimtum fī l-funduqi kulla l- layl, am ḫaraǧtum? Karīm: Did you sleep at the hotel all night or did you go out? ⁧خَرَجْنَا مَسَاءً. مَشَيْنَا فِي وَسَطِ⁩ : ⁧السَّائِح⁩ ⁧المَدِينَةِ، وَزُرْنَا الكَاتِدْرَائِيَّةَ، ثُمَّ عُدْنَا بِالمِتْرُو.⁩ as-sāʾiḥ: ḫaraǧnā masāʾan. mašaynā fī wasaṭi l-madīna, wa-zurnā l- kātidrāʾiyya, ṯumma ʿudnā bi-l-mitrū. Tourist: No, I didn't sell or buy anything. But on the subway two men were standing next to me, and there was a lot of fighting. ⁧لَا تَخَفْ. سَنَكْتُبُ مَحْضَرًا، وَسَتَأْخُذُهُ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧إِلَى قُنْصُلِيَّةِ المَغْرِبِ.⁩ Karīm: lā taḫaf. sa-naktubu maḥḍaran, wa-sa-taʾḫuḏuhu ilā qunṣuliyyati l- maġrib. Karīm: Don't be afraid. We write a report and you will take it to the Moroccan consulate. ⁧خِفْتُ كَثِيرًا، لِأَنَّنَا سَنَعُودُ يَوْمَ⁩ : ⁧السَّائِح⁩ ⁧الأَحَدِ.⁩ as-sāʾiḥ: ḫiftu kaṯīran, li-annanā sa- naʿūdu yawma l-aḥad. Interim document for the trip. ⁧مُؤَقَّتَةً لِلسَّفَرِ.⁩ What to notice. Assimilates: ⁧وَصَلْتُ⁩ , ⁧وَضَعْتُ⁩ ( ⁧و⁩ remains in the perfect), ⁧لَمْ أَجِدْهُ⁩ ( ⁧و⁩ of ⁧وَجَدَ⁩ falls into the imperfect), ⁧وَقَفَ⁩ . Concave: ⁧نِمْتُمْ⁩ , ⁧زُرْنَا⁩ , ⁧عُدْنَا⁩ , ⁧بِعْتَ⁩ , ⁧خِفْتُ⁩ (short vowel in front of consonant), ⁧لَمْ أَبِعْ⁩ , ⁧لَا تَخَفْ⁩ , ⁧قُلْ⁩ (short forms), ⁧سَنَعُودُ⁩ (long form). In this unit you learn when doubling melts, the short forms of some verbs with hamza ( ⁧خُذْ⁩ , ⁧كُلْ⁩ ) and above all the rule to write the hamza, which you need to write under dictation and to search for words in the dictionary. A week. The rule. The two equal letters are together (with the shadda) when a vowel comes later: ⁧رَدَّ⁩ , ⁧رَدَّتْ⁩ , ⁧رَدُّوا⁩ , ⁧يَرُدُّ⁩ . They separate when a consonant comes later: ⁧رَدَدْتُ⁩ , ⁧رَدَدْنَا⁩ , ⁧رَدَدْنَ⁩ . 2. The juxtaposition has two forms: ⁧لَمْ يَرُدَّ⁩ (the most used) and ⁧لَمْ يَرْدُدْ⁩ (formal, in written texts). title: Forms II and III, and liabilities
text: Lesson overview From a root the Arabic derives, with fixed patterns, new verbs from the predictable meaning: ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ • study → ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ (form II, see figure 3 below) from the root ⁧ش ر ك⁩ → ⁧شَارَكَ⁩ • To participate in the project (form III, to do with someone). You have already used many of these verbs ( ⁧يُكَلِّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُسَجِّلُ⁩ , ⁧يُسَاعِدُ⁩ , ⁧يُحَاوِلُ⁩ ); in this unity you study them systematically, with all forms: perfect, imperfect, imperative, maṣdar, participles. In the last part you learn to recognize the passive ( ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ The following entries are added: ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ "It's said to be ") very common in news. The context is the formation of a new colleague and the organisation of an open day at the Commissariat. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-17 Level A2 · Module A2.3 Complex frasi and irregular verbs Prerequisites A2-16 exceeded; root and scheme (A2-01); the four ways (A2-02 → A2-06) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 79–80 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-17), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. conjugate a verb of form II ( ⁧فَعَّلَ يُفَعِّلُ⁩ ) and of form III ( ⁧فَاعَلَ يُفَاعِلُ⁩ ) in all times and ways; 2. form maṣdar and parts: ⁧تَفْعِيل⁩ , ⁧مُفَعِّل⁩ , ⁧مُفَعَّل⁩ ; ⁧مُفَاعَلَة⁩ / ⁧فِعَال⁩ , ⁧مُفَاعِل⁩ ; 3. predicting the meaning: II = "to do" , intensive, verb by name; III = Doing with / towards someone; 4. distinguish I, II and III of the same root ( ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ , ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ ; ⁧عَلِمَ⁩ , ⁧عَلَّمَ⁩ ; ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ , ⁧كَاتَبَ⁩ ); 5. recognising the liabilities of forms I, II and III, and the staff complement ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ ; 6. describe a job and report a meeting (who attended, what was discussed, what was Decision). Two-week plan. title: Forms IV, V, VI, VII, VIII and X
text: Lesson overview In A2-17 you have studied forms II and III. Other derived forms are recognized by prefixes and schemes: ⁧أَرْسَلَ⁩ (IV), ⁧تَكَلَّمَ⁩ ( V), ⁧تَعَاوَنَ⁩ (VI) ⁧اِنْقَطَعَ⁩ (VII), ⁧اِجْتَمَعَ⁩ (III), ⁧اِسْتَقْبَلَ⁩ ( X). Many of these verbs have been using them for months ( ⁧أَعْطَى⁩ , ⁧تَعَلَّمَ⁩ , ⁧اِنْتَظَرَ⁩ , ⁧اِتَّصَلَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَطَاعَ⁩ ); Here you put them in a unique system. The objective of A2 is to recognize: given a word in a title without vowels, find the root, form and sense, and know how to read the maṣdar and the participle. News is the ideal ground: it's full of derived forms. A week. Item Details Code A2-18 Level A2 · Module A2.3 Complex frasi and irregular verbs Prerequisites A2-17 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 81 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-18), voice synthesis scripts, newspaper titles (also online), tutoring session Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the forms IV, V, VI, VII, VIII and X from the perfect, the imperfect, the maṣdar and from the participle; 2. know the most frequent value of any form (causeative, reflective, reciprocal, passive-medium, consider (s) to be (s) of the following categories: 3. recognize the assimilations of form VIII ( ⁧اِتَّصَلَ⁩ , ⁧اِزْدَحَمَ⁩ , ⁧اِضْطَرَّ⁩ ) and the difference between VII and VIII with roots in ⁧ن⁩ ; 4. recognizing verbs of four letters ( ⁧تَرْجَمَ⁩ ); 5. reading and understanding news titles without vowels. title: ‎إِنَّand the particles of his family
text: Lesson overview "In truth the language is culture" , "he said it will come," "but the problem is..." , "as if it were..." , "maybe I had time!" , "maybe it will come": a group of particles " ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ , ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ , ⁧كَأَنَّ⁩ , ⁧لَيْتَ⁩ , ⁧لَعَلَّ⁩ The following subject goes to the accusative (or is a suffix pronoun), the predicate remains at the name. ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ You know them from A2-14; here complete the family, learn why after ⁧قَالَ⁩ is used ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , and use these particles to express opinions, hopes and impressions. From the Unit A2-19 notices, titles and reading texts are without vowels or almost; dialogues and examples remain vocalized. A week. Item Details Code A2-19 Level A2 · Module A2.4 Use the language Prerequisites Test A2.3 exceeded; ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ ( A2-14); suffix pronouns (A2-10) Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 83 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-19), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use ⁧إِنَّ⁩ and its sisters with the subject of accusation or suffixes ( ⁧إِنَّهُ⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّنِي⁩ , ⁧لَعَلَّكَ⁩ ); 2. report a sentence with ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ and distinguish ⁧إِنَّ⁩ / ⁧أَنَّ⁩ / ⁧إِنْ⁩ / ⁧أَنْ⁩ ; 3. put the prepositional predicate before the subject ( ⁧إِنَّ فِي البَيْتِ رَجُلًا⁩ ); 4. recognise ⁧لَا⁩ of absolute denial ( ⁧لَا شَكَّ⁩ , ⁧لَا بَأْسَ⁩ ); 5. express an opinion, hope, desire and impression, and read a short editorial without Vowels. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the family of ⁧إِنَّ⁩ · year 1 2 Section 3: the suffixes · section 4: ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ · financial years 2–3 · vocabulary 3 Sections 5–6: order of words, ⁧لَا⁩ of absolute denial · exercises 4–6 4 Reading: an editorial · exercise 9 5 Script B: statements · writing: opinion (exercise 10) · Exercise 7–8 6 Session with the tutor: expressing opinions and hopes 7 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · Hopes and fears Friday night, shift's over. We're three weeks from Luca's departure. Arabic Transliteration Translation Hudā: kayfa tašʿur? baqiyat ṯalāṯatu Hudā: How are you feeling? They're just missing. ⁧كَيْفَ تَشْعُرُ؟ بَقِيَتْ ثَلَاثَةُ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ asābīʿa faqaṭ! Three weeks! ⁧فَقَطْ!⁩ Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧بِصَرَاحَةٍ، أَنَا مُتَفَائِلٌ، لٰكِنَّنِي قَلِقٌ قَلِيلًا.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧أَخَافُ أَلَّا أَفْهَمَ شَيْئًا.⁩ Lūkā: bi-ṣarāḥa, ana mutafāʾil, lākinnanī qaliqun qalīlā. aḫāfu allā afhama šayʾā. Luca: I'm honestly optimistic, but a little worried. I'm afraid I don't understand anything. ⁧لَا تَقْلَقْ. إِنَّ أَوَّلَ أُسْبُوعٍ صَعْبٌ دَائِمًا،⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧لٰكِنَّ الأُذُنَ تَتَعَوَّدُ بِسُرْعَةٍ.⁩ Hudā: lā taqlaq. inna awwala usbūʿin ṣaʿbun dāʾiman, lākinna l-uḏuna tataʿawwadu bi-surʿa. Hudā: Don't worry. The first week is always difficult, but the ear gets used to it quickly. ⁧سَلْمَى تَقُولُ إِنَّنِي سَأَعُودُ وَأَنَا أَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧مِثْلَ المِصْرِيِّينَ.⁩ Lūkā: Salmā taqūlu innanī sa-aʿūdu wa-ana atakallamu miṯla l-miṣriyyīn. Luca: Salmā He says I'll come back and talk like the Egyptians. ⁧لَعَلَّهَا عَلَى حَقٍّ! لَيْتَنِي أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧أَذْهَبَ مَعَكَ.⁩ Hudā: laʿallahā ʿalā ḥaqq! laytanī astaṭīʿu an aḏhaba maʿak. Hudā: Maybe he's right! I wish I could come with you. ⁧وَلِمَاذَا لَا تَأْتِينَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-li-māḏā lā taʾtīn? Why aren't you coming? ⁧لِأَنَّ أُخْتِي مَرْيَم سَتَلِدُ فِي يُولْيُو،⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مَعَهَا.⁩ Hudā: li-anna uḫtī Maryam sa-talidu fī Yūlyū, wa-urīdu an akūna maʿahā. Hudā: Because my sister Maryam will give birth in July and I want to be with her. ⁧مَبْرُوك! إِنَّ هٰذَا خَبَرٌ رَائِعٌ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: mabrūk! inna hāḏā ḫabarun rāʾiʿ. Congratulations! That's great news. Hudā: šukran. wa-anta, ḥaḍḍir Hudā: Thank you. And you pack the suitcase... ⁧كَأَنَّكَ⁩ … ⁧شُكْرًا. وَأَنْتَ، حَضِّرْ حَقِيبَتَكَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ḥaqībatak... ka-annaka ḏāhibun ilā I- it looks like you're going to the moon, ⁧ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى القَمَرِ، مِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا تُفَكِّرُ فِيهَا!⁩ qamar, min kaṯrati mā tufakkiru fīhā! How much do you think about it! What to notice. ⁧لٰكِنَّنِي⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّ الأُذُنَ⁩ , ⁧إِنَّ أَوَّلَ أُسْبُوعٍ⁩ , ⁧لَعَلَّهَا⁩ , ⁧لَيْتَنِي⁩ , ⁧كَأَنَّكَ⁩ : all particles are followed by a name to the accusative ( ⁧الأُذُنَ⁩ , ⁧أَوَّلَ⁩ ) or from a suffix. ⁧تَقُولُ إِنَّنِي⁩ : after ... say... the ... ⁧إِنَّ⁩ (Section 4). ⁧أَلَّا⁩ = ⁧أَنْ⁩ + ⁧لَا⁩ Not further worked than hot-rolled, hot-drawn or cold-rolled (cold-reduced) and not further worked than hot-rolled, hot-drawn or cold-rolled, in irregularly wound coils ⁧بِصَرَاحَةٍ⁩ "Honestly' ⁧تَتَعَوَّدُ⁩ (V) get used to it, ⁧سَتَلِدُ⁩ It will give birth to the child (A2-15: ⁧وَلَدَ يَلِدُ⁩ ), ⁧مَبْرُوك⁩ Congratulations (answered) ⁧اللهُ يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ⁩ ), ⁧القَمَر⁩ The Moon is the Moon. ⁧مِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا⁩ ... since how long... ⁧وَأَنَا أَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ I have to say that I am in favour of the Commission's proposal. ⁧وَ⁩ + pronoun describes the status (A2-20). 2. The family of ⁧إِنَّ⁩ Particle Meaning Example Translation ⁧إِنَّ⁩ (in truth), which (after ... say ...) ⁧إِنَّ العَمَلَ صَعْبٌ.⁩ Work is (really) difficult. ⁧أَنَّ⁩ which (A2-14) ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ العَمَلَ صَعْبٌ.⁩ I know work is hard. ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ why (A2-14) ⁧لِأَنَّ العَمَلَ صَعْبٌ⁩ because work is difficult ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ but ⁧لٰكِنَّ العَمَلَ صَعْبٌ⁩ but the job is difficult ⁧كَأَنَّ⁩ as if, it seems that ⁧كَأَنَّ العَمَلَ لَعِبٌ⁩ as if work were a game ⁧لَيْتَ⁩ maybe, if only (desire) ⁧لَيْتَ العَمَلَ سَهْلٌ!⁩ I wish the job was easy! ⁧لَعَلَّ⁩ Perhaps (hope or supposition) ⁧لَعَلَّ العَمَلَ سَهْلٌ.⁩ Maybe the job is easy. The rule. After these particles the subject ( ⁧المُبْتَدَأ⁩ ) goes to the accusative, the predicate ( ⁧الخَبَر⁩ ) remains at the name: ⁧العَمَلُ صَعْبٌ⁩ → ⁧إِنَّ العَمَلَ صَعْبٌ⁩ . With healthy plurals and duals you can also see without vowels: ⁧إِنَّ المُوَظَّفِينَ مَشْغُولُونَ⁩ The staff are employed. ⁧لَعَلَّ الطَّالِبَيْنِ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ⁩ . ⁧إِنَّ⁩ At the beginning of the sentence, it emphasizes (-- really, certainly) and is heard in speeches, formal texts, declarations. It doesn't often translate into English. ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ and ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ . ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ (without shadda) is a simple conjunction and can be followed by any sentence, even verbal ( ⁧لٰكِنْ لَمْ يَأْتِ⁩ ); ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ wants a name to the accused or a suffix ( ⁧لٰكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَأْتِ⁩ ). The sense is the same. ⁧لَيْتَ⁩ and ⁧لَعَلَّ⁩ . ⁧لَيْتَ⁩ expresses a desire that is often unrealizable: ⁧لَيْتَ الصَّيْفَ طَوِيلٌ⁩ Maybe the summer was long. ⁧لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ هُنَاكَ⁩ I wish I'd been there. ⁧لَعَلَّ⁩ expresses a hope or assumption: ⁧لَعَلَّكَ تَعِبٌ⁩ "Maybe you're tired" ⁧لَعَلَّهُ يَأْتِي غَدًا⁩ We hope it will come tomorrow. 3. With suffix pronouns Person   ⁧كَأَنَّلَيْتَلَعَلَّلٰكِنَّإِنَّ⁩   me / ⁧إِنَّنِي⁩ ⁧لٰكِنَّنِيإِنِّي⁩ /  ⁧كَأَنَّنِيلَيْتَنِيلَعَلِّيلٰكِنِّي⁩  you (m.)   ⁧كَأَنَّكَلَيْتَكَلَعَلَّكَلٰكِنَّكَإِنَّكَ⁩   you (f.)   ⁧كَأَنَّكِلَيْتَكِلَعَلَّكِلٰكِنَّكِإِنَّكِ⁩   him   ⁧كَأَنَّهُلَيْتَهُلَعَلَّهُلٰكِنَّهُإِنَّهُ⁩   She ⁧إِنَّهَا⁩ ⁧لٰكِنَّهَا⁩ ⁧لَعَلَّهَا⁩ ⁧لَيْتَهَا⁩ ⁧كَأَنَّهَا⁩ us ⁧إِنَّا⁩ / ⁧إِنَّنَا⁩ ⁧لٰكِنَّنَا⁩ ⁧لَعَلَّنَا⁩ ⁧لَيْتَنَا⁩ ⁧كَأَنَّنَا⁩ you (m.)   ⁧كَأَنَّكُمْلَيْتَكُمْلَعَلَّكُمْلٰكِنَّكُمْإِنَّكُمْ⁩   They (m.)   ⁧كَأَنَّهُمْلَيْتَهُمْلَعَلَّهُمْلٰكِنَّهُمْإِنَّهُمْ⁩   Both the long form ( ⁧إِنَّنِي⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّنِي⁩ ) and the short ( ⁧إِنِّي⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنِّي⁩ ). The pronoun of the situation is given. When after the particle comes a verb, you put the suffix ⁧ـهُ⁩ , which refers to nothing in particular: ⁧إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنَ السَّهْلِ⁩ ... is not easy... ⁧قَالَ إِنَّهُ سَيُسَافِرُ⁩ "He said he will leave" (here ⁧ـهُ⁩ It may also be "He"). 4. ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ : report a sentence After ⁧قَالَ⁩ and its forms ( ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧قُلْ⁩ , ⁧قِيلَ⁩ , ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ ) the "he" is ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّ⁩ : Direct speech Speech Reported .« ⁧الدَّرْسُ صَعْبٌ⁩ » ⁧قَالَ:⁩ ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ الدَّرْسَ صَعْبٌ.⁩ He said that the lesson is difficult. .« ⁧أَنَا مَرِيضَةٌ⁩ » ⁧قَالَتْ:⁩ ⁧قَالَتْ إِنَّهَا مَرِيضَةٌ.⁩ She said she was sick. .« ⁧سَنَأْتِي⁩ » ⁧قَالُوا:⁩ ⁧قَالُوا إِنَّهُمْ سَيَأْتُونَ.⁩ They said they'd come... With other verbs to say it is used. ⁧أَنَّ⁩ : ⁧أَكَّدَ أَنَّ⁩ It confirmed that the Union industry was not in a position to compete with the Union industry. ⁧ذَكَرَ أَنَّ⁩ ... he mentioned that, ⁧أَعْلَنَ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧صَرَّحَ بِأَنَّ⁩ "The Commission has stated that it is in favour of the Commission's proposal. The news is full of these formulas (A2-20 This is the subject of the report. People change, times don't. In Arabic the speech reported maintains the time of direct discourse: ⁧قَالَ إِنَّهُ مَرِيضٌ⁩ "He said he was sick" (Lett. "Who is sick" is the word. In Italian you adapt the weather. Four similar words. Word Function Example ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ... that is after ⁧قَالَ⁩ ; emphasis ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ الطَّقْسَ جَمِيلٌ.⁩ ⁧أَنَّ⁩ • • • • • • • • • • • • ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ الطَّقْسَ جَمِيلٌ.⁩ ⁧أَنْ⁩ Of, of, of, of or of a conjunction with ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَخْرُجَ.⁩ ⁧إِنْ⁩ "Se" (formal, A2-14) ⁧إِنْ تَدْرُسْ تَنْجَحْ.⁩ No vowels ⁧إن⁩ and ⁧أن⁩ are distinguished from the hamza (above or below the alif) and from what follows. 5. The order of words If the predicate is a preposition + name or adverb, it may come before the subject; the subject remains to the accused: Example Translation ⁧إِنَّ فِي البَيْتِ رَجُلًا.⁩ There's a man in the house. ⁧إِنَّ عِنْدِي سُؤَالًا.⁩ I have a question. ⁧لَيْتَ عِنْدَنَا وَقْتًا أَكْثَرَ!⁩ I wish we had more time! ⁧لٰكِنَّ مَعَهُ صَدِيقًا.⁩ But there's a friend with him. Attention: here the subject is indeterminate and accused ( ⁧رَجُلًا⁩ , ⁧سُؤَالًا⁩ , ⁧وَقْتًا⁩ ), with the alif of tanwīn. 6. ⁧لَا⁩ of absolute denial (recognize) Another word has a similar effect: ⁧لَا⁩ + name indefinite to the accused without tanwīn denies in absolute way (.......)................................................. Expression Translation ⁧لَا شَكَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ.⁩ There's no doubt about it. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ.⁩ No problem. (A1) ⁧لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ.⁩ You're welcome. (A2-10) ⁧لَا أَحَدَ هُنَا.⁩ There's no one here. ⁧لَا مُشْكِلَةَ.⁩ No problem. They are mainly fixed formulas: they are unheard of as blocks. Necessary and possible. Need expressions are used ⁧مِنَ⁩ + adjective + ⁧أَنْ⁩ : ⁧مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ تَأْتِيَ⁩ You need to be there, ⁧لَيْسَ مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ⁩ ... is not necessary to...A2-04), ⁧مِنَ المُمْكِنِ أَنْ⁩ It is possible that the following information may be provided: ⁧مِنَ المُسْتَحِيلِ أَنْ⁩ It is impossible that it should be, ⁧مِنَ الطَّبِيعِيِّ أَنْ⁩ It's normal that it is. 7. Pronunciation Double. inna, anna, lākinna, laʿalla, kaʾanna: the double consonant can be heard. With the suffixes: in-na-hu, lā-kin- na-nī, la-ʿal-la-hu. laytanī, laʿallī. ⁧ليتني⁩ and ⁧لعلّي⁩ : Attention to the short form ⁧لَعَلِّي⁩ ( la-ʿal-lī). The accuser after the particle. inna l-ʿamala ṣaʿbun: in the reading with terminations the accusative of the subject is heard; in the pause reading it remains only in the alif of tanwīn ( ⁧إِنَّ عِنْدِي سُؤَالًا⁩ : suʾālā). 8. title: Telling the Past
text: Lesson overview A story has an order (first, then, the next day, at the end), a background (it was late, it was raining, I was waiting) and events (suddenly it arrived..., it fell...), and often reports words from others (he told me that..., he asked me if...). In Arabic the background is done with ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect, events with perfect, anteriority with ⁧كَانَ قَدْ⁩ + perfect; Connectives bind sentences; ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧سَأَلَ هَلْ⁩ / ⁧إِذَا⁩ and ⁧طَلَبَ أَنْ⁩ They say the words. The context is the story of Mary's journey to Cairo and the testimony about a small accident. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-20 Level A2 · Module A2.4 Use the language Prerequisites A2-19 exceeded; ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect (A2-07); subordinate (A2-14); weak verbs (A2-15) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 84–85 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-20), voice synthesis scripts, photos of your trip, session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. order a story over time with the connectives ( ⁧فِي البِدَايَةِ⁩ , ⁧ثُمَّ⁩ , ⁧فَجْأَةً⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَئِذٍ⁩ , ⁧فِي اليَوْمِ التَّالِي⁩ , ⁧أَخِيرًا⁩ ); 2. distinguish background ( ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect) and event (perfect); 3. recognise ⁧كَانَ قَدْ⁩ + Perfect (' had done') and the state phrase with ⁧وَ⁩ ( ⁧دَخَلَ وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ⁩ ); 4. report statements, questions and requests: ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧سَأَلَ هَلْ⁩ / ⁧إِذَا⁩ , ⁧طَلَبَ مِنْهُ أَنْ⁩ ; 5. tell an event for one or two minutes and understand a short story. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: Connective · exercise 1 2 Section 3: background and event · exercise 2 · lexicon (first half) 3 Section 4: ⁧كَانَ قَدْ⁩ and the state phrase · exercise 3 4 Reading 1: one week in Cairo · exercise 10 5 Script B · Writing: Schema of a story (exercise 12) 6 Oral production: tell an event in a minute 7 Anki · review 8 Dialogue 2 · section 5: the speech reported · exercise 4 9 Section 5 (continued): questions and requests · exercises 5–6 · lexicon (second half) 10 Exercises 7–9 11 Reading 2: a chronicle · exercise 11 12 Script C · Writing: tale of 150 words (exercise 13) 13 Session with the tutor: two minute story 14 Unit verification · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · How did it go? Monday before class. Maria has just returned to Cairo with her sister for a week. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَهْلًا يَا مَارِيَا! كَيْفَ كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ahlan yā Māriyā! kayfa kānati r- riḥla? Hi, Maria! How was your trip? ⁧رَائِعَةً! فِي البِدَايَةِ كُنْتُ خَائِفَةً قَلِيلًا،⁩ : ⁧مَارِيَا⁩ ⁧لٰكِنْ بَعْدَ يَوْمَيْنِ شَعَرْتُ كَأَنَّنِي فِي بَيْتِي.⁩ Māriyā: rāʾiʿa! fī l-bidāyati kuntu ḫāʾifatan qalīlā, lākin baʿda yawmayni šaʿartu ka-annanī fī baytī. Beautiful! At first I was a little scared, but after two days I felt like home. ⁧مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا أَوَّلًا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: māḏā faʿaltumā awwalan? Luca: What did you do first? ⁧زُرْنَا الأَهْرَامَاتِ طَبْعًا. ثُمَّ، فِي اليَوْمِ⁩ : ⁧مَارِيَا⁩ … ⁧التَّالِي، ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى سُوقِ خَانِ الخَلِيلِي⁩ ⁧وَهُنَاكَ ضَاعَتْ أُخْتِي!⁩ Māriyā: zurnā l-ahrāmāti ṭabʿan. ṯumma, fī l-yawmi t-tālī, ḏahabnā ilā sūqi Ḫāni l-Ḫalīlī… wa-hunāka ḍāʿat uḫtī! The pyramids, of course. Then, the next day, we went to the market of Khān al-Khalīlī...and my sister is lost there! ⁧ضَاعَتْ؟! وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ḍāʿat?! wa-māḏā faʿalti? Luca: Are you lost?! What did you do? ⁧كُنْتُ أَشْتَرِي هَدِيَّةً لَكَ، وَفَجْأَةً الْتَفَتُّ⁩ : ⁧مَارِيَا⁩ ⁧فَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا. سَأَلْتُ بَائِعًا هَلْ رَأَى امْرَأَةً تَلْبَسُ⁩ ⁧قُبَّعَةً حَمْرَاءَ.⁩ Māriyā: kuntu aštarī hadiyyatan lak, wa-faǧʾatan iltafattu fa-lam aǧidhā. saʾaltu bāʾiʿan hal raʾā mraʾatan talbasu qubbaʿatan ḥamrāʾ. I was buying a gift for you, and all of a sudden I turned around and didn't find it. I asked a salesman if he'd seen a woman in a red hat. ⁧وَمَاذَا قَالَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-māḏā qāl? title: Travel, health, public offices
text: Lesson overview Luca's gone. In this unit you follow him to Cairo airport, luggage office, hotel, doctor, pharmacy and language center counter. These are the situations in which a traveller must be understood with simple but precise phrases: ask with courtesy ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ ...), describe an object or symptom, give your data, understand a warning and a form. The vocabulary is very concrete; grammar is what you know. Reading texts are without vowels, such as real alerts and forms. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-21 Level A2 · Module A2.4 Use the language Prerequisites A2-20 exceeded; imperative and courtesy (A2-06); Numbers, dates and prices (A2-12) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 86–87 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-21), voice synthesis script, your passport or a real form (for terminology), session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. making courteous and formal requests ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ , ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ ); 2. understand airport alerts and answer questions to passport control; 3. report lost baggage, book and register at the hotel; 4. describe to the doctor where it hurts, from when and how, and understand instructions for a drug; 5. fill out a form and solve a file at the counter. Two-week plan. title: Warnings, forms, ads, emails
text: Lesson overview An important part of the written language that you will encounter is "practical": notices on an office door, forms to fill out, ads, work emails and messages between friends. They are short texts, almost always without vowels, with fixed formulas that repeat themselves: ⁧الرَّجَاءُ عَدَمُ⁩ …, ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ …, ⁧مُغْلَقٌ لِلصِّيَانَةِ⁩ , ⁧السَّيِّدُ⁩ … ⁧المُحْتَرَمُ⁩ , ⁧تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ خَالِصِ التَّحِيَّاتِ⁩ . In this unit you learn to recognize and use these formulas, to distinguish the formal register from the informal one, and to write a full formal email. A week. title: Listen: the news and the first meeting with the Egyptian
text: Lesson overview This unit is dedicated to listening. In the first week you learn to listen to a simplified news: what to look for at first listening, how to take note of numbers and own names, what formulas come back every day ( ⁧وَفْقًا لِـ⁩ , ⁧أَعْلَنَ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ المُتَوَقَّعِ أَنْ⁩ ). In the second week you meet for the first time the Egyptian Arab, the spoken variety that you heard on the street in Cairo. The goal is only to recognize it: to understand that a phrase is Egyptian, to identify the main traits (sounds, negation, future, present with ⁧بـ⁩ ) and bring it back to fuṣḥā. In this unit nothing is produced in dialect: you always speak and write in standard Arabic. Two weeks. Item Details Code A2-23 Level A2 · Module A2.4 Use the language Prerequisites A2-22 exceeded; numbers (A2-12); ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ and speech reported (A2-19, A2-20); transliteration of names (ONO-02) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 89–90 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-23), EGY deck (recognition only), voice synthesis scripts (texts in fuṣḥā), an Egyptian player for D and E scripts, session with the tutor Audio. This book does not contain any recordings. Scripts in fuṣḥā (A, B, C) are heard with vocal synthesis or read by the tutor. Egyptian scripts (D, E) are to be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, colleague, linguistic exchange): the vocal synthesis does not reliably pronounce the dialect. Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use a strategy in three listenings (subject → data → details); 2. recognize the fixed formulas of the news and report a news with ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَعْلَنَ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧وَفْقًا لِـ⁩ ; 3. record numbers, dates, percentages and foreign names heard; 4. summarize a slow news in English; 5. recognizing the Egyptian: the sounds ( ⁧ج⁩ , ⁧ق⁩ , ⁧ث⁩ , ⁧ذ⁩ The present with ⁧بـ⁩ , the future ḥa- / ha-, denial But...-š and miš, the most frequent words; 6. Reaching a simple Egyptian phrase to fuṣḥā. Two-week plan. title: Review, simulation and dialect selection
text: Lesson overview The last three weeks of the level serve to consolidate, measure and close gaps. There is no new grammar: review the vocabulary for areas, review the grammatical framework, read three long texts partially vocized, listen to two cumulative dialogues, do an exam simulation, fill out the decision board on the dialect and, in the week 94, support the exam A2 (Part III). Item Details Code A2-24 Level A2 · Review Prerequisites Module testing A2.1 → A2.4 Exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 92–93 of the calendar), plus the exam in the week 94 Materials All volume, Anki deck A2 complete and EGY deck, reference grammar (Part V), progress log, oral simulation tutor Targets. At the end of the two weeks: 1. recognize and use vocabulary A2 of all areas; 2. apply without hesitation the grammatical framework structures of the section 3; 3. partly vocized text readings of 250–300 words at least 50 words per minute and answer questions details; 4. understand a slow news and dialogues about travel, offices and work; 5. write 150 correct words on a well-known, formal or informal subject; 6. support a prepared conversation of 12 minutes; 7. choose, with explicit criteria, the dialectal variety to study in B1; 8. pass the exam A2 (at least 70/100 and at least 12/20 in each section). Two-week plan. Week Day Activity 92 1 Vocabulary 1–6 (section 2) · Anki A2 complete 92 2 Vocabulary 7–12 · grammatical framework (section 3), rows 1–12 92 3 Grammatical framework, lines 13–24 · text 1 92 4 Text 2 · dialogue A 92 5 Text 3 • Dialogue B • Production 1 (section 7) 92 6 Examination simulation (section) 8), under real conditions 92 7 Simulation correction · list of gaps in the register 93 1–2 Lacune: return to the units indicated by the correction 93 3 Timed reading of the three texts (section 6) 93 4 Production 2 · Guided rewriting of production 1 93 5 Targeted listening and dictation on weak unit scripts 93 6 Interview prepared with the tutor (exercise 9) · decision form on dialect (section 10) Week Day Activity 93 7 Active rest: only Anki (error cards) 94 — Examination A2 (Part III) in two half days 1. How to Review Anki. Deck A2 complete every day, with a deck filtered on the wrong cards in the last 30 days. Create a card for each recurring error of the simulation (tag The EGY deck is read only, ten minutes a day at most. • Aloud. Each review text is read twice: the first in pause, the second with the endings where You're sure. • No vowels. When you read a voiced text of a unit, cover the vowels and read; Then check. • Register. Note in the Excel file the simulation scores by section: they are the basis of the plan of week 93. • Tutor. Oral simulation should be done with a native speaker: pronunciation does not evaluate itself. 2. The vocabulary A2 by areas The keywords of each area, with the unity where you studied them.
